Both are local-build artifacts, NOT defects: src/_data/site.js reads process.env.SITE_URL, netlify.toml sets it to https://drum.town, and base.njk/sitemap.njk are both gated on site.url. Iteration counter reconciled at iter 59: meta.iteration had drifted to 53 against 58 PROGRESS entries, because bookkeeping-only and repair ticks did not always bump it. Set to 59 to match PROGRESS. Side effect: 59 % 10 == 9, so the NEXT tick is a discovery pass — that is intended, the last one was iter 56.

Iteration 60, page weight: do NOT re-file the rudiments page as a byte-weight problem. It is 906 KB of raw HTML but Netlify serves brotli, which is 72 KB over the wire; the heaviest lesson is 31 KB. The real costs there are DOM node count (6,866 elements, 6,095 of them SVG primitives — content-visibility spares layout and paint but the parser still builds every node) and BL-008's unconditional 2.3 MB WAV prefetch, which is live and is ~32x the brotli'd HTML.

Iteration 60, three phantoms the orchestrator caught on itself before filing, recorded so the next sweep does not repeat them: (1) a duplicate-spec hash that omitted the articulation property, which made rock-open-hats look as though a lesson about open hi-hats notated none — it does notate them; (2) a ghost-note rule looking for a property the corpus does not have (ghosts are unaccented notes beside accented ones, so they cannot be detected that way); (3) an accent rule that matched the NEGATION in titles like "No Accents" and "Diddles Even, No Accent". Also: counting curriculum slugs without excluding section slugs produces 18 fake orphans.

Iteration 60, tooling: check-transport-reserve.js FAILS with "the harness produced no measurements" when run through the sandboxed Bash tool, and PASSES (36 measurements, 129/65px, 11px clearance) when the identical command runs from PowerShell. Edge is not the problem — it dumped a data: URL fine from PowerShell, and the same gate had passed twice earlier in the same session on the same code. Run browser-driving checks from PowerShell. Recorded in .claude/commands/improve.md step 6.

Iteration 63: a critic reported that accent:true renders no ink anywhere on the site (censusing the class "vf-articulation", which came back 0 across every built page) and concluded BL-085 chunk 1 had shipped a no-op. THAT IS WRONG. VexFlow 4 does not tag articulation glyphs with a vf-articulation class. Rendering the same spec with and without accents differs by 1,272 bytes and exactly TWO extra <path> elements for two accents, and the built page path count matches the with-accents render. Accents draw real ink, as the iteration-61 screenshots showed. Do not census VexFlow output by class name — count paths, or look at the picture.

Iteration 70, methodology for any future accessibility audit: without --force-renderer-accessibility, headless Chromium leaves content-visibility: auto subtrees uncomputed, so /rudiments/ reports 4 of 40 headings and 4 of 40 notation images in the AX tree. The screen-reader walker nearly filed that as a blocking finding. With the flag, all 40 are present at every scroll position and queryAXTree finds the fortieth card without scrolling. CONTENT-VISIBILITY COSTS A SCREEN READER NOTHING HERE — do not re-file it.

Iteration 70, the shape of nearly every gate defect found: a gate that measures the output with the thing that produced it, an exemption broader than its author realised, or a field computed and never asserted. When adding a gate, the useful question is not "does it pass" but "construct the defect it names and watch it fail" — 17 of 17 gates passed their own headline claim while failing at least one mutation of it.

Iteration 74, HOW TO MEASURE A STAFF POSITION, and the two ways it goes wrong. Stave lines render at y 58/68/78/88/98; spacing is 10, so one staff position is 5 units. The position of a note is its notehead INK BOUNDING-BOX CENTRE (exact bezier stationary points, not the control hull), which lands on VexFlow own ledger lines to under 0.001 units. NEVER measure from the raw path origin, the "M x y" that opens the d attribute: it sits 5.054 ABOVE the centre for round noteheads and 4.015 BELOW the centre for x-heads. Trap one is measuring from the origin at all, which puts every note one staff position too high and makes the snare look like a line note — that is how the orchestrator briefed reading-101 as correct and the-drum-kit as broken, when the reverse is true. Trap two is correcting it with a single constant: a uniform +5.054 fixes drums and moves every cymbal by 9.069 units, 1.81 staff positions, which would have taken the ride off the top line and turned the-drum-kit correct cymbal claims into errors. Calibrate against a ledger line for BOTH glyph families before trusting any position: c/4 and c/4/x2 both give a ledger line at y=108, a/5 and a/5/x2 both at y=48. Verified table: china b/5/x2 43, crash a/5/x2 48, hat g/5/x2 53, ride f/5/x2 58 (top line), bell e/5/x2 and high tom e/5 63 (SAME position, distinguished only by notehead shape), mid tom d/5 68, snare c/5 73 (3rd space), b/4 78 (middle line, ZERO drum uses — though 145 visible RESTS default to restKey b/4, so it is not unused ink), floor tom a/4 83, kick f/4 93, hi-hat foot d/4/x2 103. Any key census must read BOTH hands and feet and must follow grace notes, which inherit their parent keys: hands-only reports f/4 as 1 use instead of 2345, and skipping grace notes reports c/5 as 3922 instead of 4082.

Iteration 77, scratchpad collision between roles: the builder and the adversarial critic share one scratchpad directory, and the critic wrote its own mutate.js over the builder harness of the same name mid-iteration. Nothing shipped wrong, but the builder had to rebuild a 44-case suite. CONVENTION from here: name any harness or scratch script with its item id, e.g. bl123-mut-nv.js, and write temporaries under the same prefix. Both roles are told to use the same directory and neither can see the other files list in advance, so a generic name WILL eventually collide.

Iteration 79, OFFLINE AUDIO HARNESS METHOD, learned the hard way and reusable. Rendering many specs into one OfflineAudioContext by offset is fast but the offsets MUST be snapped to 128-frame render quanta: unsnapped, one probe read 1.487 at offset 0 and 1.211 elsewhere, a 19% pure artefact. Sample-snapping fixed 3 of 5 probes; quantum-snapping fixed all 5. Validate any such harness by rendering the same probe solo and at two different offsets and requiring bit-identical output, then re-render a corpus sample all three ways — the iteration-79 run got 33 of 41 bit-identical, 40 of 41 within 1.6%, and the clip verdict agreeing 41 of 41. Quote a tolerance with every peak. Validate a LEVEL metric against something set in code and not in data: footAcoustic is literally playAcousticSample("hat", …, 0.55), so a correct probe returns 0.55000.

Iteration 79, MEASURE VOICES SEPARATELY RATHER THAN BY RMS. Iteration 76 reported the acoustic ride at "roughly half the RMS" of the hat and iteration 79 showed why that is misleading: the ride PEAK equals the hat (0.9999 vs 1.0000) and the difference is length and body — energy 26.9 against 101.3, ring 2.49s against 0.14s. A single conflated RMS number cannot tell a quieter stroke from a longer one. Use peak, total energy and ring time as three separate numbers.

Iteration 79, FALSE ALARMS CAUGHT BY THE AGENTS THEMSELVES, recorded so no future sweep re-files them. (1) A duplicate-spec key omitting the grace field made all four dragadiddle exercises look identical, which reads as "the lesson about drags notates none" — #1/#2/#3 each carry 8 grace notes and only #0 ("No Drags Yet") has none. This is the SECOND time a duplicate-spec hash has produced a phantom by omitting a property; the first was articulation at iteration 60. Include every distinguishing field. (2) An accent checker resolving "beat 1" against bar 1 flagged independence-melodic-snare#1, whose "accent on beat 1" is scoped to bar 2 and sits correctly at absolute beat 5. (3) A parser mis-read "dotted-8th kick" against a spec carrying dot:true with duration 8.

Iteration 79, THE nextLessons GRAPH IS NOT A REACHABILITY GRAPH. Walking nextLessons alone from lesson 1 reaches only 106 of 217 lessons. That is a graph statistic and NOT an orphan defect: the built homepage links all 217 (219 hrefs, 217 unique) and every lesson appears in its chapter sidebar. Any future sweep quoting "111 unreachable lessons" is wrong. Related and also verified clean: 343 prerequisite edges and 336 nextLessons edges have zero dangling targets, zero section-slug targets, zero self-references and zero cycles; and difficulty is monotonic within all seven genre tracks, so the seven apparent regressions in flat curriculum order are track boundaries by design.

Iteration 79, WHAT THE PROSE-VS-NOTATION SEAM NO LONGER CONTAINS. Swept and clean, with counts, so the next campaign is aimed at something real: voice counts ("N kicks/snares/toms") 39 phrases and 0 real defects; per-voice duration claims 178 phrases and 0; title-level subdivision labels 153 and 0; sticking claims 87 explicit strings plus 45 "alternating" and 0 new beyond BL-089; sibling and graduation-criteria references 89 plus 216 and 0 dangling; graduation-criteria tempo and bar-count claims are correct BY DESIGN, since a criterion sets a target and asks the reader to loop — 27 naming a tempo above every exercise bpm are pedagogy, not defects. The seam that IS still live is meta subdivision tokens, accent POSITION claims, note-count titles and counting lines.

Iteration 81, HOW TO RUN THE CHECK SUITE, and why "all checks pass" from a tight loop is weaker evidence than it looks. Running all 22 tools/checks back to back with no gap produces transient failures across DIFFERENT checks on different runs — one run failed check-swing-feel alone, a later run failed check-nav-a11y and check-notation-frame together, and every one passed individually immediately afterward. check-notation-frame does not drive a browser at all, so this is not the headless-Edge sandbox artifact recorded at iteration 60; it looks like resource exhaustion from 22 node processes in immediate succession. A 1.5 second sleep between checks gives a clean 22 of 22. RUN THE SUITE SPACED, and if a check goes red in a tight loop, re-run that check alone before believing it. Filed as part of BL-149.

Iteration 81, A BUG CLASS FOUND BY FAULT INJECTION THAT NO GREEN RUN COULD HAVE FOUND. While hardening check-swing-feel retry path, the builder injected faults (deleting a built page, deleting ride.wav) to prove the new instrument-failure messages fire — and the first injection died with ReferenceError: __CASE_TRIES__ is not defined. String.replace with a STRING pattern replaces only the first occurrence, and that placeholder appeared twice, so the retry path called an undefined identifier. It could only ever have fired AFTER the environment had already flaked, which is exactly when a retry is needed. The lesson generalises: a retry or error path that has never executed is not tested by any number of passing runs. Inject the fault.

items.title: Listening picks over-repeat a small canon
evidence: Steve Gadd Aja x6; Weckl Master Plan, Colaiuta Ten Summoner's Tales, Porcaro Rosanna, Tony Williams Four & More, Guiliana Beat Music, ?uestlove Voodoo x4 each
items.acceptance: no single work cited in more than 3 lessons unless genuinely canonical for each (justify in log); replacements factually correct and stylistically apt; content.duplicateListeningPicks falls
log: iter 37 · 2026-08-06 · Over-cap works 7 -> 5; Aja 6 -> 5; Ten Summoner's Tales and Rosanna now compliant. THREE slots refilled, each independently fact-checked before shipping: three-limb-patterns -> Carlton Barrett / Bob Marley and The Wailers - Exodus (site's first reggae pick and first Jamaican drummer anywhere in the listening data); cymbal-voicings -> Stewart Copeland / The Police - Don't Stand So Close to Me; metronome-practice -> Papa Jo Jones / Count Basie - Jumpin' at the Woodside (1938). Round 1 was 9 proposal agents each paired with an adversarial verifier: 1 accept, 8 reject, and every rejection had the SAME shape - correct drummer, real record, note describing a technique that is not actually audible there. Round 2 re-checked the three sourced corrections the round-1 verifiers offered, on the rule that a verifier's own suggestion has not itself been checked. Copeland and Jo Jones passed on facts (attribution and release confirmed from fetched pages) but had their NOTES rewritten before shipping: Copeland's contrasted hi-hat against ride bell, i.e. two different cymbals, on a lesson about striking ONE cymbal in different places - it would have taught the wrong distinction; Jo Jones's promised an audible pedal 'chick' that a ~240bpm 1938 shellac transfer cannot deliver, and its 'cymbals parked slightly apart' detail would mean no chick at all. Ben Riley / Monk - Straight, No Chaser REJECTED outright with no safe version offered: its note described the hi-hat foot as nearly inaudible, on the one lesson whose entire subject is hearing that foot. SIX slots still cite an over-used record and were deliberately LEFT THAT WAY rather than filled with a guess: pickup-fills, fusion-sixteenth, polyrhythms-5-4, jazz-comping-foot, hiphop-louis-cole, funk-displacement. Verifiers pre-disproved Harvey Mason / Chameleon and Gadd / Aja for the sixteenth-note-carpet slot, so a later pass should not retry them. One verifier also caught two search-engine summaries carrying FABRICATED citations (a page it fetched did not mention the song at all) and discarded both, resting only on pages it read directly - see BL-063.

iter 39 · The over-cap list GREW from 6 to 8 without a single new citation being added, because two data-quality fixes removed masking. (1) Normalizing '?uestlove' / 'Questlove' / 'Questlove (The Roots)' to one spelling exposed 'The Roots — Things Fall Apart' and 'D'Angelo — Voodoo' at 4 lessons each. (2) Correcting band names to drummers merged keys that had been counted separately: 'AC/DC | Back in Black' joined the three existing 'Phil Rudd' citations (4), 'Toto | Rosanna' joined 'Jeff Porcaro' (4), and 'Miles Davis Quintet | Four & More' joined 'Tony Williams' (5). None of these are new over-citations; the audit simply could not see them before. Current over-cap: Aja 5, Four & More 5, Master Plan 4, Beat Music 4, Things Fall Apart 4, Voodoo 4, Back in Black 4, Rosanna 4. duplicateListeningPicks baseline raised 7 -> 8 for this reason and this reason only.

log: iter 38 · 2026-08-06 · SHIPPED. Header clock pill + full-width bottom dock; all 8 control ids preserved so metronome.js kept its wiring; collapsed by default at every width (dc_metro_collapsed); the session keeps ticking while collapsed and the pill dot pulses the beat (gold offbeats, ACCENT downbeat — B's red 1, verified at 1280 and true-390). Body reserve = calc(var(--transport-h) + 12px). FOUR real defects were caught after the Builder reported success, none of them visible in a screenshot. TWO by the orchestrator measuring the reserve: (a) --transport-h said 120px at <=720px while the dock rendered 129px, because the zero-height flex break element is zero-HEIGHT but not zero-LINE — being 100% wide it takes a line of its own and the row pays two row-gaps; clearance was 3px; (b) .transport__beats used flex-basis auto, so its base width grew with the beat count and 7/8 at 320px wrapped row 1, taking the dock to 181px against a 140px reserve — BL-036 recreated at the narrow end. TWO by the adversarial panel (4 lenses, 26 findings, 14 refuted, 12 survived): (c) the pill added 63px + an 8px gap of flex-shrink:0 content to a header row that already exactly filled 280px, giving every one of the 228 pages a sideways scroll below 333px and putting the hamburger fully off-screen at 280px — a WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.10 reflow regression at the normative 320px, which is also 400% zoom on a 1280px desktop; (d) .curriculum-sidebar is position:sticky sized to the viewport, so body padding slid straight past it and 65px of its scrollport sat under the dock at every desktop width — at max scroll the last entry was permanently unreachable and clicking it typed into the BPM field (verified on playing-to-a-song, jazz-elvin-jones, rock-hybrid-grooves). Also fixed from the panel: header z-index 10->60 and skip-link 20->70 so the mobile nav panel (absolute inside the header) stops being painted over and tap-stolen by the dock in landscape (was: taps at 568x320-800x360 landing on the play button and the tempo slider); .site-nav capped with max-height/overflow so a five-row panel cannot outgrow a landscape phone; reduced-motion transform kills given !important (they sat earlier in the sheet at equal specificity and were losing the cascade, so the pulse never stopped); the pill made a real toggle (it advertised aria-expanded but only ever expanded, so a second press teleported focus to the last control in the document). Accessible name rewritten: glyph/tempo/signature are all aria-hidden and nothing separated them in the rendered markup, so a composed name would have read '80beats per minute' and never said whether the click was running — one span now carries the whole name, 'Metronome, 132 beats per minute, playing', verified across a tempo change, a slider drag, start, stop and a reload with a stored tempo. Pill grows to a 44px touch target at <=860px. Three by orchestrator measurement: the 'you are here' row rendered its number in --green while its title, mark and bar were --accent, because setLastVisited always pushes the slug into visited so the row carries BOTH state classes; the mark kept its fixed 64px column when stacked, stranding a bare ○ in open space beside the minutes; and the ledger filled a 1128px container against a 720px hero, putting two measures on one page and stretching the dotted leader to 735px, further than an eye tracks from a title to its minutes (capped at 900px). items.title: Listening data: 103 of 448 entries credit a band or a non-drummer, and notes claim things that are not audible
evidence: iter 37: of 9 freshly-proposed listening picks, 8 were rejected by independent fact-checkers for the SAME defect — correct drummer, real record, but a note describing a device that is not prominent or not present on that recording

Examples caught: a 'short pickup into the downbeat' on Try a Little Tenderness where the transition was a spontaneous tempo shift and the moment described as quiet is the densest in the song; a '16th-note hi-hat carpet' on Blue Matter that is accented 8ths over a shuffle; a 5:4 claim on an album with no verified 5:4 passage
The 448 existing notes were authored the same way and have never been checked against the recordings; the base rate above suggests a substantial number make claims a listening student cannot confirm
items.acceptance: per chunk of <=10 lessons: every listening entry names the person who actually played the drums on the cited record, verified from a fetched source and refuted by an independent skeptic; the note must not repeat the artist field and must describe something audible on that record; content.listeningArtistNotDrummer falls each chunk
log: Filed at iter 37. The 8/9 rejection rate on new picks is the evidence — there is no reason to think notes written earlier are better than notes written today by the same process.

iter 39 · 2026-08-06 · chunk 1/5. NEW METRIC content.listeningArtistNotDrummer, 103 -> 81. The style guide has always said 'artist is the drummer, never the band — that is the whole point of the section', and check-listening.js claims to enforce the field contract, but it only catches a leading 'The', so 103 of 448 entries walked past it: the Elvin Jones lesson credited 'John Coltrane Quartet' and 'Elvin Jones Trio' and never Elvin Jones; the Tony Williams lesson credited 'Miles Davis Quintet'; latin-bossa-nova credited Antônio Carlos Jobim, a composer and pianist, for a record he did not drum on. Fixed 22 entries across 9 lessons (jazz-elvin-jones, jazz-tony-williams, rock-prog, rock-dynamics, metal-djent, metal-polymeters, odd-meters-9-8, ear-training, plus the Rush entry). Each attribution was researched from fetched sources and then handed to an independent skeptic told to refute it: 24 of 32 cleared, 8 held. Every applied change carried three coupled edits — artist, work ('Credited Act — Title' now that the act had left the artist field), and the note, whose leading name would otherwise have printed the drummer twice in a row. Also corrected a factual error the refuter caught in odd-meters-9-8: the Blue Rondo head is three bars of 2+2+2+3 answered by one of 3+3+3, not 2+2+2+3 throughout. Style guide amended with the only two exceptions the corpus can honor — folkloric percussion batteries with no single kit player, and programmed beats where the producer authored the drum part — both encoded as allowlists in audit-site.js. HELD, with reasons, for a later chunk: Wave (three drummers credited flat, no per-track split); Catch Thirtythree (no human kit performance — Haake programmed it, so 'Tomas Haake' alone would be false); Don Ellis 'Live at Monterey' (two drummers on one session, and the note cites a 33/16 that is not on the album); TesseracT 'Altered State' (no acoustic kit performance); Pink Floyd 'The Wall' (Mason is not on every track); Steely Dan 'Aja' (per-track drum credits — Gadd is on the title track only); latin-bossa-nova 'Chega de Saudade' (Milton Banana is right, but the existing note is entirely about Gilberto's guitar, so changing the artist alone would point a student at a drummer while telling them to listen to a guitar — the iter-37 defect class, so it was left alone rather than half-fixed).

iter 41 · 2026-08-06 · chunk 2/5. content.listeningArtistNotDrummer 81 -> 52; distinct artist strings 250 -> 238. iter 43 · 2026-08-06 · chunk 3/5. content.listeningArtistNotDrummer 52 -> 29; distinct artist strings 238 -> 229. Ten lessons, 26 attributions cleared, 4 held. This was the batch of entries earlier chunks kept deferring, and the refuters earned their keep on three of them. (1) WAVE, which chunk 1 held because three drummers are credited flat: Wikipedia's Claudio Slon article states outright that of the three, only Slon played the kit and Bobby Rosengarden and Dom Um Romão play hand percussion; Jazz Journal says the same independently. Standing hazard recorded: the Wave album page still lists three bare 'drums' credits, so a future automated pass may try to revert this to Dom Um Romão, who is a real kit player in his own right. (2) ORIGIN: the lesson cited 'Echoes of Decimation' for John Longstreth, but Longstreth was out of the band 2003-2006 and that 2005 album is James King on drums — confirmed four ways. The album was changed rather than the name, since the lesson wants Longstreth; the refuter explicitly said to apply both fields together or neither, because writing the name alone would have shipped the original error. (3) CHEGA DE SAUDADE, held in chunk 1 because the note was entirely about Gilberto's guitar: now shipped with Milton Banana and a note about the brush-and-rim kit, which is what the entry was always supposed to point at. HELD: Black Messiah (Chris Dave's contribution is real but unlocatable — Questlove is on ten of twelve cuts, Gadson has another, and no source names a track where Dave is the kit, so it cannot function as a listening assignment on a Chris Dave lesson); Jack DeJohnette / Standards Live (attribution fine, proposed work string defective); Marco Minnemann (already a drummer, not a violation); and one more. duplicateListeningPicks 8 -> 9, again with NO new citation added: correcting hiphop-chris-dave's 'Robert Glasper Experiment' to 'Chris Dave' merged it with three entries already spelled that way, so a pick that was always cited in four lessons became visible as one. Baseline raised for that reason alone. ALSO FOUND, outside the listening data and NOT fixed here: hiphop-chris-dave's bodyHtml points at tracks called 'Tabernacle' and 'Stomp Groove' as being on the 2018 Drumhedz album; neither is on its fifteen-track listing. Needs its own check.

iter 45 · 2026-08-06 · chunk 4/5. content.listeningArtistNotDrummer 29 -> 18; distinct artist strings 229 -> 222. Ten lessons, 29 attributions cleared, 2 held. This batch was mostly hip-hop, R&B and Latin, where the honest answer is often that NO drummer exists, so every entry carried a `kind` field (played / programmed / mixed / ensemble / unknown) and the refuters were told to check it as hard as the name — crediting a human for a machine part teaches a student something false about how the record was made. Results that only came out because of that field: Slum Village's Fantastic Vol. 2 is J Dilla hand-programmed on MPC pads with the quantize off, not a kit; the Pedrito Martinez Group has no drum set at all, congas and hand percussion over piano and bass; Wilfrido Vargas's record credits a TAMBORA player rather than a kit, so the entry now names Juan de la Cruz 'Chocolate' and the note tells the student which figure their tom part stands in for. TWO HELD, both because no single name honestly authors the drums: Magdalene has twelve people holding a drums credit across nine tracks and not one drum-kit credit anywhere, and Daniel Caesar's Freudian carries no drums, percussion or programming credit for anyone at all. On Magdalene the refuter rejected the researcher's proposed name but supplied a true note, and I SHIPPED THE NOTE WITHOUT THE NAME: the old text read 'Hybrid live-electronic — kit and producer-side blurred', which asserts a kit that is not on the record, on a lesson whose body uses that exact phrase to mean a drummer playing alongside triggers. Removing a false claim does not require the attribution to be settled first, and the entry still counts as a violation, so the metric is not being gamed. Also resolved by hand: eight refuters wrote PROSE into recommendWork ('RECOMMENDED for disambiguation…', 'none — bare Spiritual Unity is correct…') where the apply script expects a finished string. Three of those said to keep a bare title because 'the artist parenthetical already carries the leader' — but the parenthetical is exactly what this pass removes, so a bare title would have dropped the credited act; Spiritual Unity and Conquistador! now carry Albert Ayler Trio and Cecil Taylor, and only Motian, who IS the credited artist, keeps a bare title.

iter 48 · 2026-08-06 · FINAL CHUNK. content.listeningArtistNotDrummer 18 -> 10; distinct artist strings 222 -> 220. Campaign total: 103 -> 10 across five chunks, every change researched from a fetched page and then refuted by an independent skeptic. The TEN that remain are not unfinished work — each is a documented hold where naming anyone would be inventing a fact: Freudian carries no drums, percussion or programming credit for ANYONE; Black Messiah has three drummers, no per-track liner split, and no source naming a track where Chris Dave is the kit; Magdalene has twelve people holding a drums credit across nine tracks and not one drum-KIT credit; Catch Thirtythree and Altered State were programmed, not played; 'Human / Individual Thought Patterns' is two albums in one work string with a different drummer on each; The Wall and Night Visions credit their drummer on some tracks but not all; The Colour and the Shape needs its work split from rock-half-time's framing. The tenth is the best of them: on Bo Diddley's 1955 Checker 814 the Library of Congress National Recording Registry essay, built on three Billy Boy Arnold interviews, names the whole session and then declines on the one seat that matters — 'and a drummer, either Frank Kirkland or Clifton James.' Sources split cleanly down the middle, and Bo Diddley's own quote about who 'did the original Bo Diddley beat' is a claim about who INVENTED it, not who sat behind the kit on March 2. The historical record does not know. That is not a gap in our research, and printing either name would be a coin flip dressed as a credit. A researcher also caught a search summary handing it a fabricated personnel list for Bobby Byrd's 'I Know You Got Soul' — it fetched the cited page, found no personnel section at all, and refused to pass the credit on. Third fabrication caught by this campaign.

iter 49 · Mark REPLACED, acceptance NOT yet met. Maya's read in iter 30 was 'a record or a vinyl label first… it isn't shouting drums at me', and she was right: two concentric rings and four dots IS a vinyl label. The new seal is a snare drum in elevation — brass head inside a brick hoop, three tension rods down the shell, two lug casings breaking the silhouette, and a brass bottom counter-hoop. The Builder sketched six candidates and rasterised each at 16px rather than judging them large: a lugged hoop read as a gear, a 3/4 view read as a coin, a hoop with crossed sticks read as a cancel button. iter 51 · 2026-08-08 · ACCEPTANCE TESTED AND NOT MET. The persona milestone review asked all three, unprompted, what they took the mark to be. Beginner: 'a small wooden barrel, or maybe a honey pot… I did not read it as a drum until I'd read the word drum next to it and back-filled the meaning.' Returning player: 'a little barrel, or a tin, or one of those wooden kegs. The word drum.town sitting right next to it is what told me it was a drum, not the mark.' Keyboard user: 'a small barrel, or honestly a jar of jam.' All three separately magnified it and all three then saw a snare drum — the beginner at 340px, the keyboard user at 6x. So the geometry is right and the SCALE is wrong: at 28px the tension rods collapse into three stripes and the gold batter head reads as a lid. I OWE A CORRECTION HERE: in iter 49 I wrote that adding the bottom counter-hoop made it read as a drum, on the strength of my own look at a magnified render. Three simulated users at the real size say otherwise, and the whole point of the persona check was that my own reading is not evidence. The beginner also caught the case that makes it worse rather than better: below 360px the wordmark drops out, so the barrel is the only branding left and there is no adjacent word to back-fill from. Next attempt should design AT 28px first and scale up, not the reverse — likely fewer, heavier elements: two rods rather than three, a thicker hoop, or a silhouette that is not a vessel at all.

iter 57 · 2026-08-08 · FOURTH ATTEMPT, NOTHING SHIPPED — and that is the honest outcome, not a failure to finish. A Designer produced 27 rasterised sketches, all judged at true 16 and 28px rather than large, and delivered four finished candidates. I read the contact sheet myself at the actual pixel grid and rejected all four: at 28px they read as SHALLOW VESSELS WITH AN IMPLEMENT — ashtray with a cigarette, wok with a spatula, dark loaf with a knife. The Designer called ashtray a 'residual risk'; on the pixels it is the primary read. Candidate 4 (a cropped, open silhouette — structurally the right instinct) reads as a hamburger at 16px, which it said itself. None of the four is clearly better than what is shipped, so shipping one would have been motion without improvement. THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOW CLEAR AND IS THE REAL YIELD OF THIS TICK: the original failed as a TALL cylinder reading as a barrel; these over-corrected into SHALLOW dishes reading as pans. The misread migrated between vessel types instead of dying — barrel, honey pot, frying pan, ashtray, wok. Every closed rounded silhouette in this two-colour palette reads as a container. FOUR MEASURED FACTS worth more than the candidates: (1) --gold is 2.3:1 against the light page ground, so the CURRENT mark's largest element, its gold batter head, plus its three gold rods, are the lowest-contrast parts of the mark in the palette most visitors see — gold cannot carry a silhouette and must be treated as discardable decoration. (2) --gold against --accent is 1.35:1 in the DARK palette, so a gold head and an accent stick cannot be separated by colour at all; any crossing element needs a transparent corridor masked out of the form, showing the page ground. (3) A striking angle only reads as a strike between 28 and 38 degrees: shallower and it lies in the dish like a cigarette, steeper and it stands in it like a spoon. (4) Dead directions, each with what it actually reads as, so nobody spends another 27 sketches finding out: splayed legs = a stool; two cymbals on a rod = a fish skeleton; radiating arcs = wifi; gold centred in the head = a fried egg in a skillet; near-vertical stick = a candle on a cake; symmetric sticks = a beetle with antennae; three horizontal bands = a hamburger. Earlier rounds also killed lugged hoop = a gear, three-quarter view = a coin, crossed sticks = a cancel button. FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: stop drawing a drum in elevation. The two untried directions are an OPEN silhouette that is not a closed shape at all (candidate 4's instinct, better executed) and abandoning the drum image for something else the name affords — the word is drum.TOWN, and a mark does not have to be the instrument. Contact sheet and all 27 sketches are in the scratchpad under bl059/ for the session; the four candidate SVGs are there too if a later tick wants to iterate rather than restart.

evidence: Critic iter 23: old blanket floor 520px; new floor = 55% of natural width = 418px for a dense 760-unit 16th stave — ~20% below the old legibility minimum with ~6px sticking letters; constants 140/52/380/620/0.55 unmeasured; inline style=min-width bypasses the token system (overlaps BL-032)
items.acceptance: density-aware floor (minimum px per notated event, e.g. >=24px per 16th cell) replaces the flat 55%; constants documented with the measurement that justifies them; min-width moved to a CSS var or data attribute; verify with 390px screenshots of the densest stave (16x16ths) read for legibility
log: Filed from adversarial critique (iter 23).

iter 55 · 2026-08-08 · FIXED, and the measurement is the point. The flat floor was a PERCENTAGE of natural width, and natural width is itself capped at 1400 units for multi-bar phrases — so density got squeezed twice. Measured across the 432 staves that took a floor, it delivered between 13.6 and 116.7 px per notated event: an 8.6x spread. The dense end sat at ~5px of sticking ink, which is EXACTLY the illegibility PKG-7 fixed for single bars and silently left in place on multi-bar ones. jazz-modern-jazz#4 (72 notes, 12 bars) was the worst at 13.6px per event. Replaced with max(natural * 0.70, events * 28). Every constant is now derived and documented in .eleventy.js rather than asserted: 28 px/event comes from VexFlow writing annotations in POINTS, so 14pt sticking is 18.67 user units and rendered size is 18.67 * (pxPerEvent / 52) — PKG-7 measured 10px as legible at true 390, and 10 = 18.67 * (28/52). 52 is the renderer's own per-note allowance from its width formula. 620 is unchanged, the point below which a stave already fits a phone scroller. RESULT, measured after the change: 461 staves carry a floor, floor/natural now spans 0.70 to 1.44, and EIGHT staves floor ABOVE natural size — they scale UP and pan rather than shrinking. On rock-dynamics at a true 390px the dense frames now render a 1400-unit viewBox at 1792px, scale 1.28 where it used to be 0.70: notes 1.83x larger. Page overflow stays 0 at 280/320/360/390/480/720/1280 across four page types because the frames scroll internally. The widest floor is 2016px, which pans about 5.6 screens at 320px — a lot, and it is the trade system.md 6.5 states outright: honest panning beats illegible shrinking, and nothing is dropped at any width.

log.note: Shipped together with BL-092, because they were one defect: the row had no shedding rule, so the only shrinkable item — the site name — absorbed every deficit and clipped to "drum.tov" with text-overflow: clip, which reads as a different wordmark rather than as truncation. An explicit ladder now sheds in priority order, cheapest loss first: the nav row folds into the hamburger, then the pill meter readout, then the wordmark goes cleanly to the seal, then the theme toggle MOVES INTO the menu panel as a labelled row. The hamburger and the clock pill never shed, because below their folds each is the only route to something — site navigation, and the metronome.

Driven by @container with rem-keyed thresholds rather than more media queries. The unconditional reason, which the first justification missed: the row is capped at max-width 1200px while the viewport is not, so above 1200px a media query measures a box the row never gets. Thresholds are the row parts summed rather than chosen numbers — the model predicts a 897px min-content at a 16px root and the measured value is 897.1. Fifteen broken cells of 56 went to zero: twelve wordmark clips and three row overflows, and three of those overflows were horizontal page scroll on all 228 pages that no gate had caught.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND NO BLOCKER AND VERIFIED MORE THAN WAS ASKED: 895 cells (648 CSS cells across twelve root sizes, eight of them untested by the builder, plus 247 state cells across menu-open, dock-open, no-JS, legacy-engine and both themes), and the pill and hamburger held in every one, hit-tested at centre and both diagonal corners. It independently confirmed all three @container claims including the load-bearing one — inline-size containment does NOT hide overflow from documentElement.scrollWidth, so the existing gates stay awake — and found that container-type does not make the row a containing block for the fixed dock or the skip rail. It caught 8 of 8 mutations of the new gate.

WHAT IT CAUGHT: the fit guard listened to window resize and fonts.ready but to nothing inside the row, so changing the stored tempo from 80 to 240 — what the dock does when a reader drags the tempo slider — left the row 5px over with no shed classes until the next resize. The prescribed ResizeObserver on the row alone would NOT have fixed it, as the builder then showed: the row is block-level and its own box never changes when a child grows inside it, so it observes the row AND every element child, which means a future control added to this row is observed by construction. Also fixed: the guard stopped at clientWidth + 1 while the gate failed above clientWidth, so a guard could not always satisfy its own gate; and check-nav-a11y now asserts the menu theme row label, agreement with the header toggle, and that the text actually changes on activation — mutation-proved, since without it a broken syncToggleLabel would leave every dark-theme reader a wrong label with all 18 gates green.

HONESTY CORRECTION, made by the critic and accepted by the builder against its own headline: the 15 before/after cells were measured by setting html font-size, which models Firefox minimum-font-size, user stylesheets, extensions and devtools rather than "a reader at 150% text" generally — because this site sets html, body { font-size: 1rem } and 1rem on the root IS the browser default, so a reader changing their browser font setting moved the old media thresholds with them. The cells are real and the fix is strictly better; the population they represent is narrower than first claimed. The unconditional half of the case — the 1200px cap, and the row having had no shedding rule at all — stands untouched.

items.title: Eight dense multi-bar staves draw past their frame and widening does not converge
evidence: iter 44: rock-dynamics#1-3, jazz-modern-jazz#4, funk-modern-neo-soul#3, funk-modern-r-and-b#3, hiphop-questlove#3 and rock-studio-polish#2 draw 16-92 units past their frame today. The PKG-7 width-retry loop is scoped to sticking staves and deliberately excludes these: three passes still leave them 20-32 units over at widths up to 3057. None carries sticking, so PKG-7 is not the cause.
Suspected cause is the multi-bar 1400-unit cap rather than anything in system.md 6.5.
items.acceptance: each of the eight named staves fits inside its viewBox (check-notation-frame stays green and a new assertion covers the multi-bar path); no regression to the 852 single-bar staves; audit-lessons beat-count section unchanged
log: Filed iter 44 from the PKG-7 Builder's own measurement — it drew the boundary of its retry loop honestly rather than letting these silently ride along.

log.note: Shipped, but NOT as the item described and not as the first build implemented. The filed symptom was eight staves drawing past their frame; the actual disease was that the same eight had 95 note-on-note collisions across 42 internal barlines. On hiphop-questlove#3 bar 0 last four sixteenths were drawn ON TOP OF bar 1 first four — 90.7 units, about 3.5 noteheads — and the barline carried a run of eight X-heads at half spacing under two superimposed beams where there should be four. On rock-dynamics#1, an ACCENT lesson, the collisions printed doubled accent marks that do not exist in the spec, so a student reading accent placement off that page read the wrong pattern. Clipping hid only the fourth instance of a defect already visible three times over.

THE FIRST BUILD GREW THE VIEWBOX HORIZONTALLY — one line, no re-render, byte-exact blast radius of eight viewBox attributes and zero moved glyphs. It was correct code encoding the wrong decision: it fixed zero of the 95 collisions and merely turned three invisible notes into three orphaned ones past the closing barline. The adversarial pass measured the collisions and refuted the premise I had given the builder. The renderer own comment had ruled convergence out on numbers that were wrong: it said widening does not converge (it converges in 2-14 rounds), that the fixed point lands at 1700-1800 (measured 1043-1802), and that it costs a flat ~22% (measured 20.4-22.3% on seven and 4.1% on the eighth).

WHAT SHIPPED: generalized width convergence — the retry loop lost its hasSticking scope, depth cap 3 to 20, hard ceiling 2400, and the overflow yardstick became max(drawOverflow, rectOverflow) measured AFTER beams and tuplets draw. Collisions 95 to 5: seven of eight completely clean. Zero staves still overflow, zero hit either cap, and the viewBox backstop fired zero times. Frame-edge-to-ink gap is now 7.00 on all 932 staves with a rect as the rightmost ink every time — the same gutter every other stave on the site has. Blast radius unchanged from the first build: 924 of 932 byte-identical, exactly the same 8 changed. min-width unchanged on all 892 built staves, so BL-040 density work is untouched, and pixel spacing per event stays at 28.0 which is BL-040 own derived target — what shrinks is glyph size, 12.8px to 10.1px noteheads, and none of the eight carries sticking so PKG-7 10px floor is not in play.

ALSO FIXED, found by the critic and confirmed by the builder building the adversarial spec itself: drawOverflow did not bound tuplet-bracket ink and the comment claimed it did. Tuplet brackets are bare rect end-ticks emitted outside any vf-tuplet group and attached to no tickable, so a 4-bar phrase whose closing tuplet ends in ghost rests put 13.91 units of bracket outside the frame. Twelve real corpus tuplets already end in a rest and were safe only by luck, sitting on 760-wide single-bar staves with 7u of gutter. The new gate catches it — proved by a mutant that fails at a CONVERGED width, which is what shows rectOverflow rather than convergence is the fix. The gate parses path data independently rather than reusing drawOverflow, which is why it could catch a bug in the number the renderer widens by.

items.title: Ghost-note sticking letters say the wrong hand, and the convention has drifted corpus-wide
evidence: iter 52, found by a BL-070 adjudicator that declined to patch it in one lesson: in ghost-notes-found Ex 4 the hi-hat plays all sixteen 16ths and each ghost is CHORDED with a hat note, so the ghost is necessarily the hand that is NOT on the hat — yet all four ghosts carry sticking 'r'.

Exercises 1-3 of that same lesson use r/l strictly as hand designations with case carrying dynamics ('lowercase r/l are 1-inch ghost taps; uppercase R/L are 12-inch full strokes'), so a student reading straight through gets a physically impossible instruction.

Not local: snare-voicings#2 and finger-control#2 do the same, and finger-control#2's tip proves the drift — 'Hi-hat 16ths in the right hand, snare 16ths in the left. The r snare hits are all fingers.' The letter has stopped meaning a hand and started meaning a ghost.

ITERATION 65 GAVE THIS ITEM TEETH IT DID NOT HAVE. BL-097 now keys AUDIO DYNAMICS off the sticking case, because the corpus documents that convention in its own prose — ghost-notes-found#2 says "beats 1, 2, 3, 4 are full strokes (uppercase) and the e / & / a positions are ghosts (lowercase)", and ghost-notes-found#0 and finger-control#1 say the same. Measured over the 202 exercises that drop an unaccented drum note: 63 all-uppercase, 7 all-lowercase, 2 mixed, 130 with no sticking at all. TWO exercises are miscased against the convention and therefore play their ghosts at half volume instead of a quarter: funk-sixteenth-feel#2 and #3, both all-uppercase while their tips ask for "a ghost at roughly a quarter of their volume". The fix is their sticking case, not the gain table. I had listed stick-grip#2 as a third and the builder correctly refused it: that exercise is titled "Loud R, Soft L (Accent / Tap Demo)" and its tip asks for "taps from a low start", so its uppercase L is right and 0.5 is the level it wants — a false positive from matching ghost words in the lesson body rather than the exercise.
items.acceptance: one decision applied corpus-wide: either the letter always names the hand (and ghosts are marked some other way), or the notation documents that lowercase marks a ghost regardless of hand; every affected exercise and tip agrees with whichever is chosen; docs/content-style-guide.md records it
log: Filed iter 52. The adjudicator was right not to fix one lesson: changing it locally would have made three lessons inconsistent with each other.

log.note: Raised P2 to P1. Sticking case is no longer just a printed letter: it now decides how loud a note plays, so drift in the convention is drift in the audio.

Shipped. DECISION: a sticking letter names the hand and nothing else; ghosts carry an explicit marker. 101 lowercase letters corrected to the hand that actually plays them, 6 added, 114 ghost markers across 13 exercises in 5 lessons, player.js reading the marker instead of the case, 8 tips rewritten, new gate check-sticking-case.js, rule recorded in docs/content-style-guide.md. One documented carve-out: the grace note of a flam or drag stays lowercase, standard rudimental spelling that six lesson bodies teach by name.

THE BEST RESULT WAS UNSOUGHT: ghost-notes-found#1, titled Sixteenth-Note Ghost Stream on Snare with a tip asking for a soft hum, and finger-control#0 were playing sixteen FULL-VOLUME strokes each — measured at 1.000. Both now measure 0.250. Two ghost-note exercises that had never had a ghost. funk-sixteenth-feel#2 and #3 also improved 0.500 to 0.250, while paradiddle#0 correctly holds at 0.500 and funk-ghost-notes#0 at 0.250.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS CHECKED THE HARD PARTS AND THEY HELD: all 114 markers verified against their own tips with independent position arithmetic (sum exactly 114, no marker on a note a tip calls loud, no unmarked note a tip calls a ghost), all three continuous-hat derivations verified from the key arrays rather than the prose, and no hand assignment changed anywhere. Exactly one note in the corpus got louder, the one already named. WHAT IT CAUGHT: dynamic-spectrum#3 promised four dynamic levels and now sounds two, because putting piano above the ghosts collapsed it into mezzo permanently — the player has three tiers and two are spent on forte and fortissimo — and that had been written into a source comment no reader sees while the tip kept promising four. The style guide printed lR as a flam spelling the new gate REJECTS. And its hand rule was falsified by two exercises in the same commit where the hat is played by both hands alternating.

AND THE GATE COULD BE EMPTIED SILENTLY: deleting all 114 markers printed 0 ghost markings all well-formed and exited 0, and no check-accent-dynamics case covered a zero-accent spec, so the two exercises that went 1.000 to 0.250 were pinned by nothing and the original bug could be reinstated with all 17 gates green. Now a noaccent case measures 0.250 x16 on a spec that accents nothing, mutation-proved to fail when markers are stripped, with a staleness guard if it is ever aimed at an accented exercise; and the header says plainly it enforces well-formedness rather than completeness, that the count is a tally not a floor, and that 9 of 13 marked exercises are held by review alone.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the first build rejected parenthesized ghost noteheads as a VexFlow limitation. new VF.Parenthesis() takes position ?? LEFT so a bare constructor draws only the opener, but buildAndAttach adds LEFT and RIGHT per key and passing both draws complete parentheses — rendered at the site geometry with zero frame overflow. The conclusion survived on its second reason only, that bracketing 114 of ~750 ghosts would invent an unevenly-applied convention, which is this item own failure mode. Filed as BL-107 sequencing rather than left as a false capability claim. Also in this commit: the two exercises where every note is a ghost now print pp throughout in their meta, the convention rock-dynamics already used, which closes the only case where uppercasing left nothing visible saying quiet.

items.title: Rendered staves emit raw hex colours that escape the token system
evidence: iter 58, found by the BL-071 Builder outside its own scope: tools/notation-renderer.js sweeps black to currentColor, but ledger lines and some ancillary strokes come out of VexFlow as literal #444 and #999999. Verified independently on a rendered stave — both hex values present in the output alongside currentColor.

Harmless today because the notation ground is deliberately theme-invariant (--notation-bg / --notation-ink stay manuscript-lit in dark), so nothing looks wrong. But they are raw hex outside the token block, which the Style ledger forbids in style.css and which the renderer's own currentColor plumbing exists to prevent.
It matters the moment anyone reconsiders the theme-invariant notation ground, or adds a high-contrast mode: these two values will not follow.

items.title: The transport dock does not scale with text zoom: fixed 44px fields, fixed --transport-h
evidence: Critic measured the caption/value collision at 390px and 1280px across root font sizes. First intersection is an 18px root (BPM over 80 at +0.4px), not the 22px the CSS comment claimed. At 20px BPM/80 overlap 2.8px; at 24px 8.5px; at a 32px root (WCAG 1.4.4 200% text) BPM overlaps 80 by 20px and Beats overlaps 4/4 by 15px.

At a 32px root the damage is not only labels: the beat caption sits 7px INTO the dot row so a running beat indicator renders partly behind glyphs, the TEMPO caption overlaps the slider thumb near minimum tempo, and the select value 4/4 hangs below its own border box because height:44px and padding-top:11px are fixed while the line box scales.

What does NOT break, measured at every root from 16 to 32px: exactly two rows at <=720px and one above, dock 129/65px against a 140/76px reserve, scrollWidth === clientWidth, and all six controls still 44px tall and reachable. So this is legibility loss, not functional loss.

Root cause is that the field height and --transport-h are px constants while the text scales. The fix the critic proposes is to express them in rem (2.75rem field, 8rem/4rem dock) which is byte-identical at a 16px root and therefore keeps check-transport-reserve passing, so the dock grows with the text instead of crushing it.
items.acceptance: at a 32px root the dock captions no longer overlap their values, the dot row, or the slider thumb, and the select value stays inside its border box; the reserve still clears the dock at 16px AND at 32px, proved by a negative test that raises the root font and shows check-transport-reserve failing before the fix

items.title: Exercises omit the one notation feature they exist to teach: ghost/accent dynamics and triplets that are described in words but never notated
evidence: VERIFIED BY HAND — funk-ghost-notes#0 "1 — Funk Groove with Ghost Notes", the flagship exercise of the lesson about ghost notes. Snare falls at 16th indices 4, 6, 9, 11, 12. Its tip says "Snare on beat 2 and beat 4 is loud (the backbeat). All other snare hits are ghost notes - barely audible." Not one note in the spec carries accent:true, so the two backbeats and the three ghosts render as five IDENTICAL noteheads. A reader cannot tell from the stave which two are loud, which is the entire content of the lesson.

VERIFIED BY HAND — latin-samba-feel#3 "4 — Telecoteco Accents (Full Samba Pattern)". An exercise with the word Accents in its title, and zero accent flags in its spec. The tip promises "Two displaced accents per bar (on the &s)". Snare placement itself is correct (indices 2, 4, 10, 12 = &-of-1, 2, &-of-3, 4).

VERIFIED BY HAND — jazz-modal-comping#0 "1 — Triplet Kicks Under the Ride". Its own meta line reads "4/4 · 8th-note triplets" and spec.tuplets is null; the hands are q 8 8 q 8 8, i.e. straight eighths. The owner has corrected this exact error on this project before: quarter-note TRIPLETS in 4/4 once shipped described as quarter notes.

THE CAPABILITY EXISTS AND IS SIMPLY UNUSED HERE: 235 of 852 exercises do use accent:true and 60 do use tuplets, so this is not a renderer limit. Nor is it the ghost-note sticking-letter problem already filed as BL-078 - that is about which HAND is named; this is about no dynamic being notated at all.

CLASS SIZE, MECHANICAL, NOT YET HAND-VERIFIED: 70 exercises whose title, tip or meta claims ghost/accent dynamics while no note carries accent:true (heavily concentrated in the latin-* tracks, where bell and cascara patterns are described by their accent pattern in prose and drawn without it), and 14 that claim triplets or swing with no tuplets in a simple meter. Candidate lists in the iteration-60 discovery scratch.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: most of the 14 triplet candidates are probably CORRECT. Writing straight eighths under a "swing 8ths" label is standard publishing convention, and the meta line carries that label - jazz-ride-pattern#1, cymbal-voicings#0, hi-hat-articulation#3, jazz-waltz#0, hiphop-r-and-b-basic#1 and hiphop-j-dilla#2 all read that way. The real ones assert triplets outright rather than labelling a swing feel. Verify each before touching it.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT SWEEP (the prose-vs-notation lens) reached this class from tips rather than titles and named 14 sharp instances: hiphop-boom-bap#2, latin-modern-hybrid#0, funk-sixteenth-feel#2 and #3, funk-clyde-stubblefield#1, funk-the-meters-intro#1, funk-the-meters#1, funk-ghost-displacement#0/#1/#2, hiphop-neo-soul#0, hiphop-questlove#0, hiphop-anderson-paak#2, fusion-tony-williams-fusion#2.

SHARPEST TWO: funk-the-meters#1 says "Only the snare on beat 4 is loud — every other snare hit in the bar is a ghost note" over six identically-rendered notes; and funk-ghost-displacement#2 says out loud "beats 2 and 4 themselves must still be loud accented snares" while carrying no accent flag at all.

AN HONEST ALTERNATIVE ALREADY EXISTS IN THE CORPUS: funk-ghost-notes bodyHtml says "No accents are printed on the staff... so the whole 4-to-1 shape is yours to supply". Either notate the dynamics or say that sentence — what cannot stand is a tip asserting a hierarchy the stave silently contradicts.

ITERATION 61 MEASUREMENT, worth keeping for the remaining chunks: check-tip-claims.js contributed NOTHING to validating these 18 edits. Its regex matches 58 tips corpus-wide and its overlap with the 12 exercises of the first pass was ZERO — every one of them phrases the claim differently ("Snare on beat 2", "Backbeats on 2 and 4", "the snares on 2 and 4", "the loud snares (on 2, 4)"). audit-lessons is structurally blind here too, since accents do not change tick arithmetic, and the string "accent" appears zero times in audit-site.js. This class has no gate at all today.
items.acceptance: every exercise whose own title, tip or meta claims a dynamic distinction notates it with accent:true (or the words are corrected to match the notation), starting with the hand-verified three; a tools/checks script guards the class so it cannot silently regrow; and the triplet candidates are each individually judged against the swing-notation convention rather than swept; and a cheap second check asserts that any exercise whose tip names a loud-versus-ghost hierarchy carries at least one accent:true — the lens rates that class as zero-ambiguity

log.note: Found in the iteration-60 discovery pass, by hashing every exercise spec and asking which exercises share notation while promising different things. Three hand-verified instances, two of them unambiguous. NOTE: the same sweep produced three phantoms I caught on myself before filing - a duplicate-detection key that omitted the articulation property (which made rock-open-hats look like it notated no open hats, when it does), a ghost-note rule looking for a property the corpus does not have, and an accent rule that matched the NEGATION in titles like "No Accents". Regenerate candidates carefully.

Chunk 1 of 7 shipped: 18 exercises across 9 lessons gained accent:true on the notes their own words call loud, and 3 prose sentences that asserted the opposite were rewritten. Corpus-wide, exercises carrying any accent went 235 to 253. WHAT THE ADVERSARIAL PASS CAUGHT, and it was the whole lesson of this chunk: the first 12 edits were chosen exercise-by-exercise on tip text, WITHOUT checking the other staves on the same page, which left pages half-marked and created three new contradictions of exactly the kind BL-085 exists to remove. hiphop-boom-bap bodyHtml still said "The notation cannot show you that part. It prints six identical snare notes" directly above a stave that had just started showing it. hiphop-neo-soul #0 and #1 are byte-identical bars and only #0 got accents, so the marks appeared to vanish as a dynamic instruction. funk-clyde-stubblefield #2 and #3 are the same groove plus an open hat, under a tip saying the delta is ONE symbol. All repaired in-tick by widening to the siblings. FUTURE CHUNKS MUST SELECT BY PAGE, NOT BY EXERCISE.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, with reasons. latin-samba-feel#3: a refuting agent rejected the plan and the tip also calls the pattern cross-stick, which this data model cannot express — needs its own judgement. funk-the-meters#3: a two-bar broken backbeat whose bar 1 has NO snare on beat 2, so the beats-2-4-6-8 pattern that fits every other two-bar case does not apply; guessing there would have been the BL-086 defect in miniature. Its tip also needs reading in full. STILL OWED BY THE ACCEPTANCE: the tools/checks script that guards the class. It is deferred rather than forgotten, because the ~57 candidates still outstanding would fail it on day one; it should land with a not-to-grow baseline, in the chunk that finishes the campaign.

Dropped P1 to P2 for the remaining six chunks, deliberately and on severity rather than convenience. Chunk 1 cleared the acute cases — the flagship exercise of the lesson about ghost notes, and the two whose tips name a single loud stroke. What is left is a long tail where the WORDS ARE CORRECT and the notation is merely silent about a dynamic. BL-086 and BL-087 outrank that because the site there states something FALSE: prose that puts a voice on a beat the stave does not, and a reading lesson that teaches the wrong staff position. An omission a reader can work around; a falsehood they cannot.
Filed in the iteration-60 discovery pass by the prose-vs-notation lens. The orchestrator independently re-derived the three most severe instances from the specs before filing.

Chunk 1 of 2 shipped: 12 note moves across 9 exercises in 9 lessons, each one moving a voice from the beat the notation had it on to the beat the exercise's own title and tip say it is on. Every duration untouched — these are key moves between two existing note slots — and verified by three corpus-wide invariants: no duration changed anywhere, the multiset of keys inside each touched exercise is identical before and after (a move cannot create or destroy a voice), and only the intended 9 exercises changed at all. Fixed: independence-chapin-method#2 (snare 3 to 4, so snare + hat + hat-foot now really do strike together as the tip promises), funk-displacement#3 (snare to the e of 2 and e of 4, so the exercise is no longer byte-identical to the reference backbeat), rock-double-time#1 (snare off the downbeats to the & of 1 and & of 3), rock-prog#1, funk-purdie-intro#3, latin-mambo-intro#2, latin-songo#2, hiphop-trap#2, fusion-broken-time#2 (all four clauses of its tip are now true).

CHUNK 2 IS THE HARDER HALF, and here is exactly why. Four of the seventeen planned moves need the target beat to not exist yet, so they cannot be done as key moves and require rewriting rests and durations: jazz-broken-time-intro#3 (ride 2 to 1.5), hiphop-808-translation#0 (kick 4.5 to 3.5), hiphop-modern-production#3 (kick+floor-tom 4 to 3.5), hiphop-future-r-and-b#2 (kick 3.5 to 2.5). hiphop-808-translation#0 ALSO has a safe snare move (2 to 3) which was deliberately NOT applied: doing half of a two-error exercise would leave the page contradicting itself differently, which is the mistake iteration 61 taught. Still unexamined and also owed: four-way-foundation#2/#3/#4 (the three-exercise snare walk whose tips all say "& of 2" where the stave says beat 2) and rock-shuffle-rock#1 (title claims a kick on every beat while its own tip and spec agree on three). And the acceptance still owes the generalized check-tip-claims parser.

CHUNK-2 DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED BY THE ADVERSARIAL PASS — the earlier note was wrong twice, and acting on it would have made things worse. four-way-foundation#4: it has NO snare on beat 2 at all (snares at 1, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5) so its "& of 2" is already correct; its single error is 3.5 -> 3, the target slot exists, and its own tip confirms the target with "landing with the kick on 1 and 3" against kicks at 1 and 3. So it is a SAFE key move, not the mis-stated one. four-way-foundation#2 looks like FIX_THE_WORDS, not a note move: its tip says "still on the & of 2, but now on the & of 3 instead of beat 4" while the stave has 2 + 3.5, sibling #1 has 2 + 4, and graduationCriteria says "First variation (snare moved off the backbeat to the and of 3)" — i.e. ONE snare moves, so "& of 2" is a typo for "2" and moving the note would cement an error. #3 is genuinely ambiguous ("both off the backbeat now" argues for 2.5). rock-shuffle-rock#1 is confirmed a TITLE problem only: with its feet tuplet applied the kicks land at 1, 1.667 and 3, exactly as the tip says.

IN-TICK REPAIR after the adversarial pass, one blocking. rock-prog#1: the snare moved to the & of 1 and its accent:true STAYED BEHIND on the bare hi-hat at beat 2 — so the bar drew an accent over a hi-hat on the one beat whose tip says "not on 2 and 4 at all". My own two invariants (durations unchanged, key multiset unchanged) were both blind to it, because the accent is a non-key property and its position sequence was byte-identical. Accent and snare indices now match at [1,7]. Also fixed: rock-prog graduationCriteria still named the old second hit (1.5 + 4, now 1.5 + 4.5); the chapin#2 tip called beat 4 "the ride quarter" when beat 4 is an eighth and the quarters are beats 1 and 3; and hiphop-trap#2 got visible:true on the rest the floor tom vacated, since an invisible rest left a blank with no symbol. I REJECTED the critic's alternative fix there (swap so the hat sounds on 4 and the tom alone on 4.5) because it would have moved the HI-HAT from 4.5 to 4, changing a voice rhythm no title, tip or lesson body asks to change.

Chunk 2 of 2 shipped, and the campaign is closed. The harder half: four exercises needed rests and durations rewritten because the target beat did not exist yet — hiphop-modern-production#3 (kick+floor-tom to the &-of-3), hiphop-future-r-and-b#2 in 5/4, hiphop-808-translation#0 (kick to the &-of-3 plus the snare move chunk 1 withheld), and jazz-broken-time-intro. Plus four-way-foundation#4 (a safe key move), four-way-foundation#2 (fix the words: its "& of 2" was a typo for "2", proved by its own graduationCriteria saying ONE snare moves), four-way-foundation#3 (judged FOR the move to 2.5 on three independent clauses), and rock-shuffle-rock#1 (title only). audit-lessons stayed byte-identical through all of it, which is the sharp edge when durations change.

THE BUILDER REFUSED MY INSTRUCTION ON jazz-broken-time-intro#3 AND WAS RIGHT. I briefed a ride move from beat 2 to 1.5; it declined, arguing the ride pattern is 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 4.5 and never uses 1.5, and that the lesson thesis is subtraction so bar 1 must be a subset of bar 2. I verified both. Moving that note would have invented one. BUT the adversarial pass then found it had pinned the wrong side of the same page: exercise 3 was titled "Skip Notes Only (No Quarters)" while playing 2, 2.5, 4, 4.5 — and the site defines the skip note in jazz-ride-pattern as the second, swung 8th, so the skips are 2.5 and 4.5. Exercise 3 was byte-identical to exercise 2, made the lesson three-step build a no-op, and falsified its own graduation criterion. The tip written that round described a wrong stave accurately. The stave is now 2.5 and 4.5 only, the three-step build is real (minus beat 3, then minus 1 and 3, then skips only), and the lesson body was rewritten too — it had described a quarter on beat 2 that the ride pattern does not contain.

items.title: Twenty exercises put a named voice on a different beat than their own words say
evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED, three of three checked reproduced exactly. independence-chapin-method#2 is titled "3 — Single Snare on Beat 4" and its tip promises "Snare on beat 4 — landing WITH the ride quarter and the hi-hat foot. Three things at once on that beat." The snare is chorded at beat 3. The hat foot is on 2 and 4. The unison the exercise exists to teach happens nowhere in the bar, and it is the only step out of place in a graded walk whose siblings (and-of-2 = 2.5, and-of-4 = 4.5, a-of-4 = 4.667) are all correct.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. funk-displacement#3 "4 — 16th-Shifted Backbeat": the tip says "snare on the e of 2 and the e of 4, one 16th off the home position" (2.25 and 4.25). The spec puts the snare at exactly 2 and 4. The displacement is ZERO — the entire subject of the exercise is absent from the stave.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. rock-double-time#1: tip says "snare on the and of 1 and the and of 3 ... Notice the snare does not land on the downbeats." Spec has the snare at 2 and 4, which are exactly the downbeats it tells the reader it avoids.

CORROBORATED FROM A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DIRECTION: hashing every exercise spec found funk-displacement#3 and rock-double-time#1 sitting in a group of EIGHT exercises that share one byte-identical plain 16th-hat backbeat. Several of that group are legitimate feel exercises (the same notation played behind or ahead of the click, which cannot be notated); these two are not. The duplication is the mechanism — a reference spec was reused where a displaced one was needed.

REPORTED BY THE LENS, NOT YET RE-VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR (11 more): rock-prog#1 (half the asymmetry missing), funk-purdie-intro#3 (snare at 2.5 not 3, and its bodyHtml calls a 1-bar spec a four-bar preview), hiphop-808-translation#0, hiphop-modern-production#3, fusion-broken-time#2, jazz-broken-time-intro#3, latin-mambo-intro#2, latin-songo#2 (tip says cross-stick "still on 2 and 4", spec moved it to 3.5), hiphop-future-r-and-b#2, hiphop-trap#2, latin-mozambique#1.

PLUS four-way-foundation#2/#3/#4, a three-exercise snare walk whose tips all say "and of 2" where the stave says beat 2 — and #2 says "still on the and of 2" when no earlier exercise ever put it there.

The lens hand-checked 111 position lists and cleared 94. The dominant false-positive sources it documents are contrastive clauses ("not on 2 and 4", "no snare on 2", "Beginners want to add a snare on 2; resist"), bar-scoped tips over multi-bar specs, and explicitly-unnotated voices ("the crash lives on beat 1 of the next bar (not shown)").

LESSON FOR THE REMAINING CHUNKS, learned the hard way in chunk 1: verifying that durations and key multisets are unchanged is NOT sufficient. Moving a key between slots leaves every other property behind, so an accent, an articulation or a visible-rest flag can end up on the wrong note while both invariants still report clean. Any future move must carry the note's other properties with it, or explicitly decide not to.

Shipped. reading-101 told beginners the snare sits on the MIDDLE LINE. It sits in the middle SPACE, third from the bottom — and b/4, the middle line, has ZERO drum uses across all 852 exercises, so the lesson that teaches reading was pointing at the one position on the stave that is always empty. Two more claims in the same lesson were wrong with it: "Toms sit between snare and hi-hat in pitch order" is false for the floor tom (a/4 at y 83, BELOW the snare at 73), and the corpus draws the hi-hat above the top line rather than sharing the ride position. the-drum-kit was correct throughout and was left alone, including its hand-drawn diagram, whose SVG geometry the critic verified glyph by glyph. The rewrite states all nine positions the lesson covers and turns the empty middle line into a teaching point rather than a silence: "No drum is written on the middle line itself, so the snare space sits just above it."

A THIRD LESSON WAS WRONG AND I HAD NOT FLAGGED IT. rock-tom-grooves said most of the rhythmic activity "sits below" the snare, on the high tom (e/5), mid tom (d/5) and floor tom (a/4). The high tom at 63 and the mid tom at 68 are ABOVE the snare at 73; only the floor tom is below. The builder found it in the corpus-wide sweep the acceptance demanded rather than in the two lessons the item named. Four more were fixed on my instruction after the adversarial pass: metal-quarter-bass said two kicks are "notated on the same line (f/4)" under its own Notation Note heading, where f/4 renders in a SPACE, and rock-cross-stick, hiphop-r-and-b-basic and transcription-method each said cross-stick is "notated on the snare line". The rule applied, and now recorded: a sentence is a position claim when it pairs line or space with either a concrete key or the verb notated in a notation context. The bare possessive idiom — "the snare line", "a busy kick line", meaning a part rather than a stave line — is correct English and all 57 instances of it were deliberately left alone. Six lessons against the 10-lesson cap.

THE GATE THIS ACCEPTANCE OWED, AND THE FIRST ONE IN THIS PROJECT TO SURVIVE AN INDEPENDENT MUTATION AUDIT. tools/checks/check-staff-positions.js derives the position table from rendered SVG on every run — including the stave line positions themselves, so a stave-geometry change re-derives rather than silently shifting every claim — and asserts position claims, ordering claims (a collective "toms" must hold for EVERY member), that the middle line carries no drum voice, and a coverage floor. Final: 35 claims across 7 lessons, floor 32, 22 mutation cases with 20 caught and 2 controls correctly green. The builder fixed two real holes its own harness found: a clause naming a second voice after the position was skipped as ambiguous, and b/4 was skipped by the middle-line rule precisely BECAUSE it has no player voice, so a middle-line note sailed past the one rule written to catch it. The critic then ran 41 mutations of its own and found NO UNDOCUMENTED HOLE — all six documented holes reproduce exactly as documented. Iteration 70 mutation-tested all 18 gates and rated zero as protecting what they claim; this is the first to clear that bar. Every number in the gate header was re-derived from what the code computes rather than patched, after the critic found four of them wrong.

THE BUILDER REFUSED A FALSE GREEN RATHER THAN BANKING IT. Re-running the mutation harness produced one case reporting PASS where FAIL was expected — an apparent hole in the gate, discovered after the critic had already signed off. It did not report that as a hole and it did not quietly drop the case. It read the patch: the mutation set centre = span.minY + 5.054, the ink TOP plus a constant, not the raw path origin plus a constant. Every notehead VexFlow emits here is exactly 10.108 units tall for both glyph families, so half the height IS 5.054 and minY + 5.054 lands on the true centre for every key. The mutation injected no defect, so green was correct and the harness had mislabelled its own patch. The variant that matters — raw origin plus a uniform constant, which is the mistake I actually made — is caught, on c/4/x2 at 117.069 against a ledger line at 108. That is recorded in the gate header as a trap for the next auditor.

I BRIEFED A WRONG CONSTANT AND BOTH AGENTS CAUGHT IT. I measured positions from the raw path origin, got every note one staff position too high, and concluded the snare was a LINE note — which would have made the-drum-kit, the lesson that is correct, look like the one needing repair. I caught that much myself with a ledger-line check and briefed the builder with a "+5 correction". That was still wrong: the offset is +5.054 for round noteheads and MINUS 4.015 for x-heads, so a uniform +5.054 fixes drums and moves every cymbal by 9.069 units, 1.81 staff positions. The builder refused it and derived both; the critic reproduced both to under 0.001 units against VexFlow ledger lines. Had my constant shipped, the ride would have come off the top line and the-drum-kit cymbal claims would have been "fixed" into errors. Recorded in meta.discoveryNotes so the next iteration pays nothing for it.

Shipped as an ARMED state rather than continuous audio, because browsers block an AudioContext without a user gesture on the current document and the click that navigated belongs to the previous one. dc_metro_running lives in sessionStorage; on load, if it survived, the dock expands (without overwriting the collapse preference), the go button gains a brass ring and the accessible name "Play, resume metronome at N BPM", and a status line reads "Paused. Press play." The /metronome/ copy now states the limitation instead of implying the sound follows you.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND A BLOCKER THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED: nothing listened for pageshow, and every page here is bfcache-eligible. Because an armed page holds no AudioContext at all (getCtx is lazy), a Back navigation restored the document verbatim and the arming code never re-ran — giving both a missed arm (idle dock, flag still set, i.e. the exact pre-fix behaviour, now intermittent) and a stale arm (a restored page still reading "Paused. Press play." when nothing was paused). Fixed with a pageshow handler guarded on event.persisted and on session being null. The critic could not reproduce it because headless Edge does not enable bfcache by default; the builder then proved it in both directions with real restores under --enable-features=BackForwardCache.

Also fixed in-tick: collapsing an ARMED dock now clears the flag and disarms, so a reader who has finished practising has a dismissal that survives navigation — before this the only route to clearing it was press-play-then-stop, and their collapse press also durably flipped the collapse preference the one-load override existed to protect. The status line gained a line clamp because it silently lost the word "play." at a 20px root font. And a pre-existing bug found while proving the fix: on a back_forward navigation that MISSES bfcache the browser re-applies its own form state after metronome.js restores from localStorage, so the dock reported 4/4 while beatsPerBar, the dot row and the accent pattern were all 3. autocomplete="off" on the four dock controls. Kept in this commit rather than split out because it directly falsifies the "your tempo and meter still set" promise this item just added.

items.title: The running click dies on every page navigation, which is the difference between a practice tool and a demo
evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED IN SOURCE: metronome.js persists only dc_metro_bpm, dc_metro_ts, dc_metro_vol and dc_metro_collapsed. The session is a module-scope variable plus an AudioContext, both destroyed on unload. The file header states it outright: "Each page navigation reloads the page, so the playing state resets."

The persona set 90 BPM, pressed play, tapped through to the rudiment they wanted, and got silence. In a room with a kit and the phone propped up, they said they would have opened their phone's metronome app instead — which for that goal is the same as leaving.

Measured: loading a page carrying exactly what a playing session leaves behind (dc_metro_collapsed=0, dc_metro_bpm=90) restores the open dock and the tempo, but the go button reads play, its label reads "Start metronome", and the accessible name reads "Metronome, 90 beats per minute, stopped".

The /metronome/ page closes by saying "The metronome follows you to every lesson on the site, so any exercise you open is one click away from being practiced properly." The dock follows; the click does not. The sentence is literally true and quietly concedes the point, but it reads as a promise that it keeps going.

BL-076 makes this worse rather than overlapping it: because the dock will not adopt the exercise tempo, the reader pays the full tempo-entry cost again after every navigation. BL-076 is within a page; this is across pages, and BL-076 acceptance does not cover it.

CONSTRAINT THE IMPLEMENTER MUST DESIGN AROUND, NOT DISCOVER: browsers block an AudioContext from producing sound without a user gesture, so a naive "resume automatically on load" cannot work. The honest shapes are a one-tap resume that is obvious and pre-armed, or a persistent-session architecture that does not reload.

CAVEAT ON THE EVIDENCE, stated by the walker: they could not drive a live cross-page navigation with audio actually running, because headless Edge stopped producing DOM output mid-session. The finding rests on the source and on a real-browser load of the persisted state, not on a live observation, and they said so rather than claiming it.
items.acceptance: a reader who starts the click and then navigates either keeps hearing it, or is one obvious tap from resuming it at the same tempo — and no copy on the site promises more than the implementation delivers
