items.title: Playback ignores accents entirely, so a ghost note and a backbeat come out at identical volume
evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED IN SOURCE. player.js scheduleVoice() calls kit[drum](c, t, out) with no velocity or gain derived from the note. The string "accent" does not appear anywhere in src/assets/js/player.js. Every stroke in a pattern is played at the voice function's own fixed peak gain.
tools/notation-renderer.js:114 DOES draw the accent (a ">" articulation above the note), so the two channels disagree: the stave can say loud and the audio cannot.

This is the companion half of BL-085 and arguably the worse half. On funk-ghost-notes#0 — the flagship exercise of the lesson about ghost notes — the tip asks for "a 4-to-1 ratio between accented and ghosted snare". Today the notation renders all five snares identically AND the playback sounds all five identically, so a learner has no way to perceive the ratio from the site at all, in either channel. Fixing only BL-085 leaves the audio still lying.

The machinery is half there already: hatElectronic(c, t, out, gainScale) takes a gainScale argument, so at least one voice can already be scaled. The other voice functions take (c, t, out) and would need the same parameter.
The site's own homepage premise is "real notation and audio playback", and dynamics are the one thing a drummer practises hardest.
items.acceptance: a note carrying accent:true plays audibly louder than an unaccented note of the same voice, in both the electronic and acoustic kits, with the ratio chosen to match what the lessons ask for (funk-ghost-notes asks for roughly 4-to-1); unaccented notes in a bar that marks accents are treated as ghosts and play softer still, or the lessons stop claiming a hierarchy the audio cannot produce; no exercise gets louder overall than it is today

log.note: Found while tracing what accent:true actually affects downstream, before starting the BL-085 content edits. The trace also turned up that check-tip-claims.js:133-138 changes its interpretation once a bar marks accents (unaccented c/5 hits become ghosts and stop counting), which is correct behaviour but means BL-085 edits must be re-gated; and that its exemption map carries hiphop-anderson-paak#2 with the comment "bar has ghost strokes but marks no accent:true, so the ghost filter cannot fire" — that exemption exists because of BL-085 and should be removable once that exercise is fixed.

Shipped. One GainNode per (note, key) between the voice and the session master, created only when the level is not 1, so the 26 voice functions are untouched and an accent-free spec builds byte-for-byte the graph it built before. Three tiers: an accented note and every note of a voice this spec never accents play at 1.0 (so nothing is boosted); an unaccented snare or tom of an accented voice is a ghost at 0.25; an unaccented cymbal or kick of an accented voice is a tap at 0.5. Measured with OfflineAudioContext against the shipped data-spec on the built page: attenuation lands on exactly 0.250 / 0.500 / 1.000, giving 4.00-to-1 on funk-ghost-notes#0 electronic and 3.97-to-1 acoustic — the ratio its tip has always asked for and the audio never delivered.

TWO THINGS THE ADVERSARIAL PASS CHANGED, AND THE FIRST WAS A REAL BLOCKER. The builder applied 0.25 to all 190 exercises that lower a drum note, and defended it by claiming paradiddle#0 and ghost-notes-found#2 have structurally identical specs so nothing readable could separate them. They are not identical: the sticking case separates them, and the corpus documents that convention in the very exercise cited — ghost-notes-found#2 says "beats 1, 2, 3, 4 are full strokes (uppercase) and the e / & / a positions are ghosts (lowercase)". 62 exercises were whispering at 4-to-1 while the letters printed under their own staves called those strokes full, on the accent-tap shelf and the most-trafficked rudiment lesson on the site. An uppercase-sticking veto sends those to 0.5: paradiddle#0 went 5.24 to 2.62, matching its tip which asks for "slightly louder", while both ghost lessons and both new prose sentences stayed exactly where they were.

The second change was to the claim, not the code. Both comments said nothing anywhere could come out louder. False: samples are signed and the mix is a linear sum, so attenuating one of two partially-cancelling contributions can raise a peak — four exercises peak higher and the worst note-window rise is 1.0187. What is actually invariant is RMS, which fell in 201 of 201 accent-lowering exercises, so the gate now asserts RMS rather than peak. That measurement also caught a bug in the gate: its LOUDER_TOL was 1.002, below the 1.019 cancellation ceiling, so it would have failed correct code the moment a case covered funk-james-brown#3. An unclaimed win worth recording: 196 of 201 of these exercises already peaked past full scale, up to 2.172, and this change reduces that clipping — latin-mozambique#1 2.094 to 1.487, funk-new-orleans#3 1.850 to 1.184.

New gate check-accent-dynamics.js, the fifteenth and the first that can hear anything. It renders each case twice — shipped and with accent stripped — so it needs no baseline: an accent-free spec marks no voices and creates no gain node, and therefore IS the old behaviour reproduced from current code. Nine cases across ghost and tap tiers, snare/tom/kick/hi-hat voices and both kits, asserting attenuation against each note own accent-blind peak rather than a cross-note ratio (a paradiddle accent already reads 1.31x its own taps in the accent-blind render purely from burst summation, so cross-note ratios measure the exercise as much as the code). Ten mutants run, nine caught; openHatBypass passes and is documented as a named blind spot because no corpus exercise has an unaccented open hat in a hat-accenting spec, making that mutant behaviourally identical to correct code today. Exits 0 with a loud SKIP where no browser exists, ~2s.

UNPROVEN, NOT WORKING — owner report, 2026-08-16. Dylan still hears no volume difference on accented exercises. This item acceptance was measured and met as written, but it measured an ISOLATED snare line with the hi-hat keys dropped so nothing would mask the attack, which proves the gain node and not the experience. In the real mix sixteen hi-hat 16ths at full volume play over a ghost at roughly -12 dB. Superseded by BL-153, which owns the in-mix verification, and gated behind BL-152, which asks whether the deployed player.js contains this code at all — assets ship unversioned, so Dylan may never have received it. Do not cite the 4.00-to-1 figure as evidence that a reader can hear an accent.

items.title: Pages scroll sideways at large text sizes, and a CSS comment claims they do not
evidence: Measured during BL-091 across 13 widths x 3 meters x 4 root font sizes, armed and idle in the same document: at a 24px root, 3 of 39 cells overflow by up to 12px; at a 32px root, 9 of 39 cells overflow by up to 211px. The figures are IDENTICAL armed and idle, so this is page-level and pre-existing, not the transport dock.

style.css:1813 currently asserts the opposite — that a 32px root produces no sideways scroll at any width. That is the same class of false in-repo claim the loop has now corrected three times in prose and twice in comments.

Related to but wider than BL-069, which names .ledger__title on the homepage below 480px as one offender. A 211px overflow is far more than one flex item, so there are other offenders not yet identified.

A third data point from the iteration-60 persona walk, not yet chased: at 280px with a 32px root the page scrolled sideways by 20px and the offender measured there was a notation SVG in an exercise (532px wide, right edge 570px), while .site-header__inner measured exactly 280. Note the iteration-44 builder previously DISPROVED a similar claim about notation SVGs at normal text size, so verify before believing it.

ITERATION 69: the header is exonerated. A 648-cell sweep (54 widths x 12 root sizes) found headerCulprits = 0 at every overflowing cell, so the remaining sideways scroll at raised text is entirely content: h2.ledger__title on the homepage, .listening__count and .lesson-row a on lesson pages, and the rudiments cards. BL-064 fixed three header-caused overflow cells that no gate had caught; what is left belongs here and to BL-069.
items.acceptance: no page scrolls sideways at a 32px root at any width from 280 to 1600, or the CSS comment is corrected to state exactly which widths and roots do overflow and by how much; every offender is identified by measurement rather than assumed

log.note: Filed from a measurement taken while proving something else. The armed-vs-idle control is what makes it trustworthy: the overflow is identical in both states, so BL-091 did not cause it.

Closed with BL-069. Both halves of the acceptance are met: no page scrolls sideways at a 32px root at any width in the range (verified to 1599px, and to a 40px root, on 2700 cells), AND the false comment is corrected. The comment was not at the line I briefed — it is in the TRANSPORT DOCK CAPTIONS block, and it claimed there is no sideways scroll at any width, which was a statement about the PAGE that the dock block had no standing to make and which was false when written: /metronome/ scrolled 18px at 280/@40 and the homepage 208px, neither of them the dock doing. The dock is now exonerated by measurement instead of by assertion — not a culprit in a single one of the 810 cells — and page-level overflow is owned by a new SIDEWAYS SCROLL CONTAINMENT block that carries the real numbers.

THE ITEM PUNISHED ITS OWN FIX TWICE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF IT. First: the new block asserted in capitals that the default text size does not move, on a grid too sparse to have caught the .btn regression it was hiding — the same class of unbacked in-repo claim this item exists to remove, re-introduced inside the block closing it. Second: the block said 104 of 810 cells overflowed. Independent re-measurement gives 26 core + 82 broad = 108, and the builder own sweep artifacts on disk give the same 26 and 82; 104 was not reproducible from anything. Corrected, with the split stated. The section heading is now bounded as SIDEWAYS SCROLL CONTAINMENT (roots 16 to 40) rather than reading as an unqualified promise, and the 48px failure is named in-comment as filed elsewhere rather than quietly implied to be handled.

AND A THIRD TIME, ON RE-REVIEW OF THE REWORK. The corrected block quoted the root-48 failures as 10 cells with independence-chapin at +23px on span.chip — the critic own numbers from the artifact it had reviewed BEFORE the rework. Two of the four rule changes moved them: dropping .btn flex-wrap reopened /metronome/ at that root, and moving .chip to min-width: 0 took independence-chapin to +46px on `a` and removed span.chip as a culprit anywhere. Re-measured against the shipped sheet it is 20 of 300, and the comment now says so and says why the old figures were wrong. Two smaller ones fixed with it: the stated grid did not sum to its stated total (280 to 480 in steps of 16 is 13 widths, not 14, and two wide cells were undisclosed — the arithmetic is now spelled out to 350 + 30), and three box counts were off by one from a sentinel key in the builder map (1336/1336/486 against real HEAD is 1335/1335/485). The 695,961 figure could not be independently verified and is now stated as roughly 700,000. Three rounds, three classes of unbacked in-repo number, all in the package written to end unbacked in-repo numbers — recorded because that is the honest lesson of this item and not a footnote to it.

items.title: Nineteen exercises say "ride" and notate a hi-hat, including the lesson that teaches the ride pattern
evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED corpus sweep: 19 exercises across 8 lessons have the word "ride" in their title, tip or meta while their hands array contains only g/5/x2 (hi-hat) and neither f/5/x2 (ride) nor e/5/x2 (bell).

independence-chapin-method is the worst case — all five exercises. Its bodyHtml states the lesson's premise as "lock the ride and hi-hat foot into their jazz roles", exercise 1 is titled "The Foundation: Ride + Hi-Hat Foot Alone", and every stave draws that voice as a hi-hat. The hi-hat FOOT is separately notated as d/4/x2 in the same exercises, so the hand voice is unambiguously meant to be the ride.
jazz-ride-pattern#0 "Quarters on the Ride", #1 "Add the Skip-Note (the Ride Pattern)" and #3 are the same defect in the lesson whose entire subject is the ride pattern.

Also: three-limb-patterns#0 "Pair: Ride + Hi-Hat Foot", #1, #4 "Three-Limb Combo C: Hi-Hat + Kick + Ride"; independence-clave-foot x3; four-way-foundation#0 "Three Limbs First (Ride + Hat Foot + Kick)" and #1; the-shuffle, latin-guaguanco, rock-open-hats one each.

A reader following the notation plays a hi-hat where the lesson means a ride — and in a jazz independence lesson that is the difference between the exercise working and not. It also renders on the wrong staff position, so it teaches the wrong reading too.

CAVEAT FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the sweep matched any mention of the word, so passing references ("you could move this to the ride") will be in the 19 and are NOT defects. Read each tip. rock-open-hats and latin-guaguanco are the likeliest false positives. three-limb-patterns#4 also carries a separate, already-filed voice confusion (BL-089).
Found while fixing BL-086 in the same lesson: distinct defect class (wrong instrument, not wrong beat) so it was filed rather than folded in, and the BL-086 fix stands on its own.
items.acceptance: every exercise whose words name the ride notates the ride, or its words are corrected to say hi-hat — decided per exercise by reading the tip and the lesson body, not by sweeping; the change is visually verified because it moves noteheads to a different staff position and changes which voice plays

log.note: Filed during BL-086 chunk 1. Noticed because independence-chapin-method#2 tip says the snare lands "WITH the ride quarter" while the notation had no ride at all, then confirmed as a corpus-wide class by sweep.

Chunk 1 of 3 shipped: the two lessons whose entire subject is the ride. jazz-ride-pattern (all four exercises) and independence-chapin-method (all five) had every hand notehead on g/5/x2, a hi-hat, while their words named the ride throughout — "Quarters on the Ride" notating a hi-hat, and a jazz independence lesson whose stated premise is "lock the ride and hi-hat foot into their jazz roles" drawing the hand as a hat while separately notating the hi-hat FOOT as d/4/x2 in the same exercises. So there was no reading on which the hand voice was correct. 47 source lines changed, g/5/x2 to f/5/x2. That is 58 noteheads, not the 48 first reported — 46 literal note objects plus a generator at L5419 emitting 12 more, counted two independent ways by the adversarial pass.

THE BUILDER EXTENDED MY SCOPE BY ONE AND WAS RIGHT. I briefed eight exercises; it changed nine, adding jazz-ride-pattern#2 "Add the Hi-Hat Foot on 2 and 4" — which my sweep missed because its own tip says "hi-hat foot" rather than "ride". The lesson body prescribes the build order literally: "Quarters first. Add the skip-note. Add the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. Add the bass drum on 1." So #2 is #1 plus a foot with the hand voice unchanged, and fixing only #0/#1/#3 would have put three steps of a four-step progression on the top line and the fourth in the space above it — worse than the status quo, and a direct failure of the acceptance, which says decided by reading the tip AND THE LESSON BODY. That is the third time a builder on this loop has overruled the orchestrator and been right.

NO PROSE NEEDED REPAIRING, WHICH IS THE UNUSUAL SHAPE OF THIS BUG. Every "hi-hat" in both lessons refers to the FOOT and every "ride" was already true of the intent, so the notation was the only liar. Verified rather than assumed: an orchestrator diff of HEAD against the working tree, parsed per slug, shows 217 slugs before and after, exactly 2 changed, 9 exercises, and ZERO prose or metadata changes anywhere in the corpus. Normalising the diff by swapping the key back makes every added line byte-identical to the line it replaced, so no duration, dot, rest, accent or sticking moved — which is what a voice change must look like. chapin#4 "the ride is written as straight triplets for clarity" survives and is now literally about the ride rather than vacuous.

MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED. Geometry: every hand notehead in all 9 exercises now sits at y=58, exactly the top line, against reference probes of g/5/x2=53 and f/5/x2=58, with glyph identity confirmed by SVG command sequence so they are still x-heads and only the snare and kick are round. Audio: player.js maps f/5/x2 to the ride, and all 9 exercises rendered through the real player in an OfflineAudioContext against their pre-change specs give 0 of 18 renders unchanged — the change reached the ears in both kits. jazz-ride-pattern#0 electronic moved its sub-1kHz energy fraction from roughly 0.010 to roughly 0.175 — the builder measured 0.0113 to 0.1776 and the critic 0.0099 to 0.1727 with an independent filter, same direction and magnitude — landing on a single-note ride probe. Decay times were reported but NOT independently verified, so they are not recorded here as fact. And the fix puts these lessons onto the site own documented convention: reading-101 states "hi-hat in the space above the top line, ride on the top line". Before this, jazz-ride-pattern and its own downstream lesson jazz-medium-swing taught the same pattern on two different staff positions; they now render identically.

TWO AUDIBLE CONSEQUENCES WORTH RECORDING, NEITHER A REGRESSION. In the ACOUSTIC kit the change roughly HALVES RMS across all nine exercises — jazz-ride-pattern#0 from 0.0470 to 0.0241, chapin#4 from 0.0899 to 0.0510 — because the acoustic ride sample is much quieter than the acoustic hat. That is a global property other lessons already inherit rather than something this change introduced, but these nine get noticeably quieter for acoustic-kit readers and someone should listen. And chapin exercise 5 now plays twelve ride strokes per bar at 75 BPM with a ride long decay where it previously played twelve short hat ticks; its tip already owns the notation choice ("the ride is written as straight triplets for clarity"), so the page stays honest, but it is the one exercise where the change is more than a different drum. Also an asterisk on the no-prose-repair claim: jazz-ride-pattern listening[2].note says "the hi-hat on 2 and 4 is quiet, constant, and completely load-bearing", the only "hi-hat" in either lesson not explicitly qualified as the foot. It describes an Oscar Peterson record rather than the notation, and in jazz it means the foot chick, so it is not falsified — but the claim needed the footnote.

CHUNK PLAN REVISED FROM 2 TO 3, because the builder corrected sweep found more than either of us had. four-way-foundation is 5 exercises and not 2 — #2/#3/#4 continue the same hand voice under a graduation criterion reading "ride 8ths, hat-foot 2 and 4, kick 1 and 3, snare 2 and 4" — and two lessons were invisible to an exercise-words sweep entirely because no individual tip says the word: independence-melodic-snare (4 exercises, graduation criterion "holds shape over the ride + hat-foot scaffold", and it is chapin own nextLessons target) and fusion-coordination-foundation (1, body says "The ride plays a jazz pattern"). Chunk 2 = three-limb-patterns #0/#1/#4, four-way-foundation #0-#4, independence-clave-foot #1/#2/#4 (11 exercises). Chunk 3 = the two new lessons (5). DO NOT SWEEP three-limb-patterns: its #2 and #3 are deliberately the hi-hat, "the rock starting pair", and changing them would be a new defect. And three-limb-patterns#4 needs more than a voice change — its title names "Hi-Hat + Kick + Ride" while only two voices are notated, and once the hand becomes the ride there is no hi-hat on that stave at all; that is the BL-089 overlap.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT FOR CHUNKS 2 AND 3, discovered by the adversarial pass on BL-123 and binding on whoever takes them. check-named-voices holds seven of the remaining exercises by their LESSON graduation criteria rather than per-exercise, because those exercises never say "ride" in their own words — which is exactly why the original BL-099 sweep missed them. The hazard: fixing ANY ONE exercise in such a lesson satisfies the lesson-scoped criterion, which retires the grad exemption, which takes the tripwire with it. Ten exercises are covered by nothing but a grad entry — three-limb-patterns#2 and #3, four-way-foundation#2/#3/#4, independence-melodic-snare#0-3, fusion-coordination-foundation#0 — and once that entry is deleted there is no miss left to exempt and nothing to re-add. THEREFORE: each of the five remaining lessons must be converted ATOMICALLY, in one commit, never exercise by exercise. Also note the critic could not reconcile the "16 exercises" figure: it counts the five lessons as holding 20 exercises, 18 of them hat-only-with-no-ride, and only 8 saying "ride" in their own words. Re-derive the number before planning the chunk rather than trusting either figure.

Chunk 2 of 3 shipped: three lessons converted WHOLE, 11 exercises, 108 noteheads g/5/x2 to f/5/x2. three-limb-patterns #0/#1/#4, four-way-foundation all five, independence-clave-foot #1/#2/#4. Orchestrator-verified against HEAD per slug: 217 slugs both sides, exactly 3 changed, 11 exercises, and prose moved in one lesson only. 79 of 82 changed source lines are byte-identical after swapping the key back, so again nothing but the instrument moved.

THE ATOMICITY RULE HELD, AND TWO EXERCISES WERE CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE. three-limb-patterns#2 and #3 are titled "Pair: Hi-Hat Hand + Kick on 1 and 3" and "Combo B: Hi-Hat + Kick + Snare (Rock)" and stay on the hi-hat, because the lesson graduationCriteria carries TWO TRACKS — "Ride + hi-hat foot 2 and 4 + snare on 2 and 4" and "Hi-hat hand + kick 1 and 3 + snare 2 and 4 (rock-style three-limb)" — so it deliberately teaches a jazz track and a rock track on one page. Sweeping them would have destroyed a teaching structure rather than fixed a defect. Verified untouched and still rendering at y 53 while the converted staves sit at y 58. independence-clave-foot #0 and #3 were likewise left, being foot-alone with no hand voice. And no graduation criterion needed rewording anywhere: three-limb [0], four-way [0] and clave-foot [1] all became TRUE for the first time rather than needing to be softened.

THE RETITLE WAS FORCED BY THE GATE, NOT CHOSEN. three-limb-patterns#4 went from "Hi-Hat + Kick + Ride" to "Ride + Kick + Hat Foot", because after the swap the bare word "Hi-Hat" in the title matches neither g/5/x2 nor d/4/x2 anywhere in that exercise and becomes a NEW unexempted miss — and check-named-voices exemptions may only shrink. The builder named all three limbs rather than only the two drawn, because the exercise is "Three-Limb Combo C" and its sibling "Combo B" titles all three, and because the new title names the same un-notated voice the tip already names, so BL-089 defect count is unchanged at one. The tip parenthetical "(notated on the hi-hat line — read it as the ride)" was deleted as mandatory: check-staff-positions rule 5, widened last iteration, reads that sentence LITERALLY and its own comment predicted this exact moment.

A TRAP THE BUILDER IDENTIFIED AND AVOIDED, WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS COUNTERINTUITIVE. The obvious honest fix for the un-notated hat foot on three-limb-patterns#4 — adding "(not notated above; play them)", exactly as independence-singing#0 does — WOULD HAVE RETIRED THE BL-089 EXEMPTION, because "not notated" is a DISPLACED marker inside the 45-character window and would have exempted the mention by rule. So the gate punishes that particular honest disclosure. The hat-foot sentence was left byte-identical instead, and BL-089 keeps its tripwire. Anyone fixing BL-089 or BL-125 needs to know this before reaching for the same wording.

CHUNK 3 OF 3 — CAMPAIGN CLOSED. 54 noteheads across the last five exercises: independence-melodic-snare #0-#3 and fusion-coordination-foundation#0. Both lessons were the dangerous kind, held ENTIRELY by their lesson graduation criteria because no exercise own words say "ride" — which is exactly why the original sweep missed them — so both had to be converted atomically and both were. Orchestrator-verified against HEAD per slug: 217 slugs both sides, exactly 2 changed, 5 exercises. The builder pure-swap proof holds again: 54 lines differ by the key alone and are byte-identical after swapping it back, and a whole-file census moves only two counts, g/5/x2 4800 to 4746 and f/5/x2 1124 to 1178.

NO PROSE WAS FALSIFIED — THE CHANGE MADE FALSE SENTENCES TRUE. independence-melodic-snare body already opened "Once the ride, hi-hat foot, and kick are stable... the snare hand is free" and its graduationCriteria[0] already said "over the ride + hat-foot scaffold"; fusion-coordination-foundation body already said "The ride plays a jazz pattern". The hand was a ride in every sentence either lesson wrote and a hi-hat in every notehead either lesson drew. Five tip clauses were ADDED, one per exercise, to close the BL-127 exposure the conversion creates: each is true of its own stave, hedge-free, and verified by the gate to read as a CLAIM rather than an exemption. Three of them also created new true position claims that check-tip-claims now enforces.

THE BUILDER CLOSED A HOLE THE ORCHESTRATOR DID NOT BRIEF. It added all five exercises to KNOWN_CLAIMED, reasoning that the freshly written tip clauses are now the ONLY thing binding these staves — so if one is later reworded into a hedge, or a rule widens to swallow it, the exercise stops being checked with NO MISS TO SHOW FOR IT, because the ride genuinely is notated and nothing would look wrong. KNOWN_CLAIMED fails instead. That is the same failure mode iteration 77 built KNOWN_CLAIMED for, applied by the builder to its own new work without being asked.

AUDIT METHOD, AND A CORRECTION TO IT THAT MATTERS FOR EVERY FUTURE AUDIO CHECK. The builder verified the change by instrumenting fetch, decodeAudioData and createBufferSource on the SHIPPED player.js, driven by the data-spec lifted from the BUILT page, and counting sample-file URLs: ride.wav x6/12/18/12/6 against a reverted control. The conclusion is right and the critic reproduced it — but THE METHOD AS STATED CANNOT ESTABLISH IT. footAcoustic plays the SAME hat_closed.wav as the hand voice, separated only by a 0.55 gain node (player.js:369-371), so a URL count cannot tell the hi-hat foot from a leaked hand voice; it worked only because the residual count happened to equal the foot count. The control figures also silently summed the two rather than being hat_closed x8/16/24/16/8. THE SOUND METHOD IS GAIN-RESOLVED INSTRUMENTATION: every residual carries gain 0.55 and hat_closed at gain 1.0 is EXACTLY ZERO in all five shipped exercises, which is decisive, and structurally so too since zero g/5/x2 remain in either lesson. Record that, not the URL count. Both remain better than spectra: iteration 79 found a metric with ride at 0.1555 and hat at 0.1858, overlapping and useless, and iteration 76 mis-read the acoustic ride as half the RMS of the hat when its peak is identical.

FINAL CAMPAIGN TALLY, measured by reverting every converted exercise one at a time and putting it to the gate: 25 EXERCISES ACROSS 7 LESSONS over three chunks — jazz-ride-pattern #0-#3 and independence-chapin-method #0-#4 (chunk 1, iteration 76); three-limb-patterns #0/#1/#4, four-way-foundation #0-#4 and independence-clave-foot #1/#2/#4 (chunk 2, iteration 78); independence-melodic-snare #0-#3 and fusion-coordination-foundation#0 (chunk 3). Two exercises — three-limb-patterns #2 and #3 — keep their hand hi-hat DELIBERATELY, because that lesson graduation criteria carry two tracks, one jazz and one rock, and sweeping them would have destroyed a teaching structure. Exemptions went 20 to 7 across the campaign. 24 of the 25 are individually bound: reverting any one alone turns check-named-voices red.

THREE NUMBERS CORRECTED AFTER THE ADVERSARIAL PASS, AND THE BUILDER THEN CORRECTED BOTH THE CRITIC AND THE ORCHESTRATOR. (1) The reported gate delta quoted the file own stale iteration-77 header; measured current-gate against pre-change content it is 3403 to 3412 mentions and 2045 to 2053 pairs, so +9 and +8 — not the +15/+11 first reported nor the +10/+9 the critic and orchestrator measured, because the fcf#0 rewrite below removed a "hi-hat foot" mention after they had both measured. (2) "Byte length unchanged" was true of the SWAP and stated as if it were the file: the 54 key-swap lines contribute zero bytes because g/5/x2 and f/5/x2 are the same width, while the file grows 417 bytes from the five prose lines, 1,980,339 to 1,980,756 LF-normalised. The builder earlier figures were UTF-16 code units from String.length rather than bytes, in a file full of em dashes, quarter-note glyphs and middots. (3) check-tip-claims coverage is 311/227 to 313/229, so TWO of the five now carry a second independent binding beyond check-named-voices, not three — the fcf#0 rewrite gave up its own.

ONE CLAUSE WAS A MARKER AND WAS REWRITTEN. The critic judged fusion-coordination-foundation#0 added sentence near-verbatim the lesson own body ("The ride plays a jazz pattern... The hi-hat foot lands on 2 and 4") against a style guide that says a tip carries COACHING. The builder agreed and replaced it with something the body never explains — the body asserts the &-of-4 snare is "the entry point" and never says why it is the easy one to install first: "That pickup doubles the second note of the ride ding-a, so both hands land together and the placement comes free." True note by note, since hands[5] is the chord f/5/x2 plus c/5 at the &-of-4, and it borrows phrasing this lesson prerequisite chain already teaches in independence-chapin-method#1. The other four clauses stood: ims#1 "only the snare line changes" names what is invariant, and ims#3 scaffold note is genuinely useful in a sparseness exercise. Recorded because the alternative offered was explicitly allowed — an honest marker beats invented coaching — and the builder chose neither.

items.title: hiphop-808-translation exercise 2 is a byte-identical duplicate of exercise 1 and notates none of the floor tom it is named for
evidence: JSON.stringify of hands is IDENTICAL between hiphop-808-translation#0 and #1, and so is feet. Verified by the adversarial pass during BL-086.

items.acceptance: exercise 2 notates the floor tom doubling the kick as its title and tip describe, and is no longer a duplicate of exercise 1; both exercises snare positions agree with the lesson premise and its siblings

log.note: Found by the adversarial critic while checking whether BL-086 chunk 1 left any page half-fixed. Filed rather than fixed because it needs new notation written, not a note moved.

Closed inside BL-086 chunk 2, because leaving it would have left the page half-fixed. hiphop-808-translation#1 was a byte-identical duplicate of #0 titled "Floor-Tom-as-808 Sub Layer" with no floor tom in it. items.title: Changing the meter mid-click resets the accent phase to the wrong place in the bar
evidence: metronome.js sets session.beatsPerBar on a meter change while beatIndex keeps counting, and scheduleAhead accents when beatIndex % beatsPerBar === 0. So switching 4 to 6 mid-run puts the next downbeat 1 to 5 clicks away instead of on the bar, and the accented 1 — which the dock design calls the whole point of the beat row — lands in the middle of a bar until the counters happen to realign.

Pre-existing on the time-signature select path. Found by the adversarial pass during BL-076, which noted that the new per-exercise tempo handoff multiplies exposure by 892: every handoff that changes the meter while a click is running hits it.

The fix looks like one line — zero beatIndex when the meter changes during a session — but it needs a decision about whether the bar should restart immediately or at the next bar boundary, and a real-browser check that the beat dots and the pill lamp both follow.
items.acceptance: changing the meter while the click is running puts the next accented beat on a bar boundary, verified in a real browser by sampling the beat-dot classes across the change; the beat row and the pill lamp agree

log.note: Filed by the adversarial critic during BL-076. Pre-existing, not caused by that change, but that change made it far more reachable.

Shipped. scheduleAhead accents beatIndex % beatsPerBar, and setMeter reassigned beatsPerBar while leaving beatIndex counting, so the accented 1 landed wherever the counter happened to fall. Measured on the built site before the fix: a 6/8 to 4/4 change at 100 BPM waited 1200ms for its first downbeat, a 2/4 to 7/8 change waited six clicks, and a 5/4 to 3/4 change at 30 BPM waited FOUR SECONDS. The dot row told the same lie — 6/8 to 4/4 ran 1 2 3 4 5 (blank) 3 4 1, and 5/4 to 3/4 jumped from dot 4 straight to dot 2. Fixed by zeroing session.beatIndex on a real meter change, so the next NEWLY scheduled click is the downbeat.

THE GUARD ON THAT RESET IS THE PART I WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WRONG. I briefed "reset the phase" without qualification. adoptTempo calls setMeter on EVERY press of every exercise tempo button, and 832 of those name a meter the dock is frequently already in, so an unconditional reset would have restarted the bar under a reader sitting in 4/4 who pressed "Metronome 90" beneath a 4/4 exercise — turning a fix for a rare mid-bar accent into a common one. The builder guarded it on v !== session.beatsPerBar and made the same-meter handoff a gate scenario. Type safety of that comparison was checked separately: setMeter opens with Number.isFinite(v), which does not coerce, and both call sites pass parseInt results, so v and session.beatsPerBar are always numbers and !== cannot misfire.

TWO MORE DEFECTS ON THE SAME CONTROL, FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN BY THE ITEM. (1) A click committed under the old meter fired into a shorter row, beatDots[5] was undefined, and the pill lamp pulsed ALONE for a full 88-96ms flash — the dock disagreeing with itself in peripheral vision, which is the one thing the beat row exists to be trusted about. Fixed by clamping the index to the last dot: those clicks are the tail of the outgoing bar and the last dot is where that reads, and index 0 is in range for every row the dock can build, so a clamp cannot invent a false downbeat. (2) renderBeats rebuilt the row without clearing the pill, leaving the lamp holding is-downbeat-active for 24ms over four dark dots; both faces now go dark together. The clamp also repairs a prefers-reduced-motion path: style.css strips the scale transform for those readers and leaves colour alone to carry the beat, so before the clamp they lost the beat row entirely for out-of-range clicks rather than merely losing the animation.

THE GATE: tools/checks/check-metro-phase.js, the 20th check. It serves _site over loopback and drives the real built page in headless Edge through 10 scenarios, swapping AudioContext and requestAnimationFrame on the iframe window — both resolved by metronome.js at call time, so no source change was needed to make it testable. Accent truth is read from the oscillator FREQUENCY and beat truth from the dot classes, and it reads SCHEDULE_AHEAD out of the built script so the window it reports cannot drift from the code. Necessary because the headless audio clock advances 0.0000s while performance.now advances 1500ms under --virtual-time-budget, and rAF fires zero callbacks in that time. Mutation audit: 29 mutants, 29 of 29 as expected — 23 defects caught, 6 controls correctly green — including the original bug, an unconditional reset, reset-to-1, reset-on-grow-only, the clamp reverted and three wrong clamps, setBpm resetting phase, and SCHEDULE_AHEAD raised past its own bound. Adds ~13s to the suite.

THE ADVERSARIAL PASS BLOCKED THE GATE, NOT THE FIX. It verified all three code edits as correct and would have shipped them: it reproduced every defect measurement independently, and it swept a single meter change across the whole bar in 1/10-beat steps — 50 positions across three meter and tempo combinations — getting 50 of 50 landing the first newly scheduled click on an accent, with zero row/pill disagreements across all 65 scenarios it ran. What it blocked on was hygiene and honesty in the new check. (1) The harness was written to the _site ROOT, which .claude/commands/improve.md forbids explicitly and notes has already cost two ticks: audit-site.js walks every .html and skips only a top-level dev/, so the harness counts as a page with no main landmark and no skip link and bumps pageCount. Three newer browser checks do it correctly; this one copied check-transport-reserve, the oldest and the one the note was written about. (2) The tempo scenario asserted NOTHING — deleting session.bpm = bpm left the gate green while the running click ignored tempo changes entirely, intervals staying at 0.6s instead of 0.375s, and the gate printed "a tempo change left the phase alone". That is the computed-and-never-asserted shape the iteration-70 audit catalogued. (3) The header claimed "every run is identical" against six runs measuring 217/216/216/216/214/217 clicks, with a three-click tolerance that would flake red before a push. All fixed, and the false claim is the same class BL-098 existed to remove.

MEASUREMENTS CORRECTED AGAINST THE CRITIC RE-MEASUREMENT. The committed comment said 24ms of pill-alone over four dark dots; the critic reproduced 24ms over a SEVEN-dot row, and the case that actually matches four dark dots measures 56-80ms and comes from a SAME-METER handoff landing 30-60ms into a downbeat flash — so the number understated its own defect roughly threefold and named the wrong row. And "4 of 14 change events carried a committed accented click" is 3 distinct events of 13: the check drives 13 control changes, not 14, and two of the four marks were the same stale click counted twice, 72ms apart in the rapid scenario. The critic also corrected the reduced-motion claim: the dot keeps a box-shadow ring under prefers-reduced-motion, so those readers were not uniquely harmed — before the clamp an out-of-range click lit NO dot at all for every reader, which is the real and larger finding.

items.title: 44 exercises play at a tempo that contradicts the tempo printed on them
evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED across all 892 specs. The exercise meta prints a tempo against a note-value glyph, and player.js reads the same number as a QUARTER-note rate regardless of the glyph. 44 exercises disagree with themselves as a result.

41 of them are marked with a DOTTED QUARTER, e.g. double-paradiddle#0 "6/8 · ♩. = 80". One 6/8 bar is two dotted quarters, so the printed tempo means a 1.5s bar. The player treats 80 as quarters and plays 3 quarter-units, i.e. a 2.25s bar — the audio is 50% SLOWER than the marking printed directly above it. Affects all four 6/8 rudiment lessons (double-paradiddle, six-stroke-roll-found and siblings) and the 6/8 latin material.
3 are marked with an EIGHTH: reading-time-signatures#3 "6/8 · ♪ = 160" and #4 "12/8 · ♪ = 180" plus one more. The player reads 160 as quarters, so the audio runs at TWICE the printed tempo.
Some compound-meter metas are correct and must not be swept: rock-odd-meter#1 prints "8th = 200" against bpm 100, which is exactly right. The fix has to read the glyph, not the meter.

tools/checks/check-exercise-meta.js cannot see any of this: it matches /♩\s*=\s*(\d+)/ and compares the number to spec.bpm without knowing which note value the glyph names. The 40 dotted-quarter metas do not even match its regex, so they are silently skipped (777 checked, 40 skipped).

Found while deciding what BL-076 tempo handoff should do on x/8 pages. It is pre-existing and NOT caused by that change — and it is a third, independent reason the handoff correctly omits those pages, because there is no single tempo on them to hand over.
The site premise on the homepage is real notation AND audio playback. An exercise whose audio contradicts its own printed tempo by 1.5x fails that on both halves at once.

MECHANISM CORRECTED AT ITERATION 70 by mutation-testing the gate: check-exercise-meta does NOT "compare the last number without reading the glyph". Its regex is a bare quarter glyph, and it cannot match "♩. = 80" at all because the dot sits between the glyph and the equals sign — so `tempos` comes back empty, `declared` is null, and the whole comparison block is skipped. All 40 dotted-quarter metas are therefore not merely mis-compared but never compared, while still being counted in the gate "all 852 exercise metas match their spec" line. Rewriting all 40 to a tempo three times wrong still exits 0.
items.acceptance: every exercise sounds at the tempo printed on it: either the meta glyph is corrected to the note value the player actually counts, or the player and pattern-math learn the glyph, decided per exercise by reading the meta rather than sweeping; check-exercise-meta.js is extended to parse the note-value glyph so the class cannot silently regrow, and it stops skipping the 40 metas its regex currently misses

items.title: Draw ghost notes as parenthesized noteheads — the renderer can, and 750 of them are invisible
evidence: BL-078 gave the data an explicit ghost marker and 114 notes now carry it, but tools/notation-renderer.js does not read the field at all — it is not even in the noteSpec JSDoc. A stave draws notehead, beam, accent, sticking letter, open-hat "o" and grace notes, and nothing else. So a ghost is audible and invisible.

For 11 of the 13 exercises BL-078 touched this is fine or better: the accents mark the loud strokes, so the ghosts read as the bare notes, which is real notation rather than the private lowercase convention it replaced. The gap is the exercises where a ghost sits among unaccented full strokes.

THE CAPABILITY EXISTS AND WAS WRONGLY RULED OUT. The BL-078 builder prototyped VexFlow parentheses and rejected them because only the opening bracket drew. The adversarial pass found why: new VF.Parenthesis() takes position ?? LEFT, so with no argument it can only ever draw the opener. VexFlow 4.2.5 own buildAndAttach adds TWO modifiers per key, LEFT and RIGHT, and passing both explicitly draws complete parentheses — rendered and screenshotted on four real exercises with beams, accents and the sticking row intact.

MEASURED COST AT THE SITE OWN GEOMETRY: rightmost ink moves from 746.7 to 746.7-747.0 user units against a stave end of 752.0 and a viewBox of 760, across all 12 sticking-bearing exercises. Zero overflow; check-notation-frame is not at risk.

THE REAL REASON TO SEQUENCE IT, and it is a good one: only 114 of roughly 750 unaccented drum strokes carry the marker today, so bracketing just those would invent an unevenly-applied convention — the exact failure BL-078 exists to end. This should ship WITH or AFTER the pass that marks the remaining ~636 across 59 lessons, not before it.
items.acceptance: every note the data calls a ghost is drawn as a parenthesized notehead, and every note drawn plain is one the data does not call a ghost — so the convention is applied evenly corpus-wide; no stave overflows its frame and check-notation-frame still passes

items.title: The dynamics lessons teach five levels and the player has three, with nothing on the page saying so
evidence: dynamic-spectrum#3 tip: "One bar, four dynamic levels. Beat 1: forte (accented). Beat 2: piano. Beat 3: mezzo. Beat 4: fortissimo (accented)." The player produces 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 1.0 — beats 2 and 3 are identical in the audio and identical on the page, both bare R.

This is structural, not a bug: the player has three tiers (accent 1.0, tap 0.5, ghost 0.25) and two are spent on forte and fortissimo, so piano and mezzo must collapse. dynamic-spectrum#4, titled "The Dynamic Ladder (climbing through all 5 levels)", has the same problem across bars.
PARENTHESES CANNOT FIX THIS, so BL-107 does not cover it: a bracket is binary and these exercises need piano separated from mezzo separated from ghost.

The missing notation is DYNAMIC TEXT. VexFlow 4.2.5 ships TextDynamics, and notation-renderer.js already places annotations TOP (the open-hat "o") and BOTTOM (the sticking row), so the placement machinery exists. It is standard music notation rather than a private convention, and it touches 2 exercises rather than 13, so the uneven-convention objection that sequences BL-107 does not apply here.

The corpus already prints whole-bar dynamics in the meta line — rock-dynamics reads "4/4 · ♩ = 90 · pp throughout" — and iteration 67 used that convention for the two exercises where every note is a ghost. What is missing is a dynamic that varies WITHIN a bar.
Interim: BL-078 fixed the tip so it no longer promises four levels the audio cannot produce. The lesson still teaches five and the site can sound three.

items.title: Three exercises assert a right hand that appears nowhere on their stave

items.title: One bar still collides with its neighbour because every bar gets the same width regardless of density
evidence: jazz-modern-jazz#4 bar5|bar6 still overlaps by 80.5 units across 5 notes after BL-065 convergence cleared the other 41 of 42 barlines. It is the only one left.

Root cause is barWidth = innerWidth / bars in notation-renderer.js: every bar in a phrase gets an equal slot no matter how many events it holds. A bar of sixteen 16ths and a bar of four quarters are given the same room, so a dense bar overruns while a sparse one wastes space. No total width fixes that — the critic and the builder independently reached the same conclusion, and convergence at any width leaves this one bar colliding.

The fix is proportional bar widths: divide the inner width by each bar tick count rather than by the bar count. That is a real engraving change to the multi-bar path, so it needs its own visual verification across the 153 multi-bar specs, not a rider on another item.

Cheap guard worth having either way: BL-065 added a frame check that asserts ink is inside the FRAME, and it is structurally blind to ink inside the frame but on top of another bar. A check asserting ink stays inside its own BAR would have caught all 95 collisions years ago.
items.acceptance: no note in any multi-bar stave overlaps a note in an adjacent bar, verified by measuring glyph boxes against bar boundaries across all 153 multi-bar specs; a check asserts it so the class cannot silently regrow

log.note: Filed as the residue of BL-065. Both the adversarial critic and the builder identified the same root cause independently and both declined to fix it inside that item, correctly — it is an engraving change, not a width change.
Filed by the iteration-70 discovery pass: a mutation audit of all 18 gates ("audit the auditors"), plus the first screen-reader walk of the site.

Shipped. Clipping of 332 staves below and 66 above went to 0 on all four edges. The renderer now measures true ink — exact cubic and quadratic stationary points, sampled arcs, real rect and text boxes, plus the half-stroke VexFlow adds because d is a centerline — and grows the frame on all four edges; the gate got an independent full-box parser on both axes sharing no code or constants with it. 382 frames grew, 0 shrank, 0 changed WIDTH, so natW is untouched and all 494 density floors are byte-identical and BL-040 is undisturbed. The change is purely framing: strip the viewBox and the auto-ids and all 852 lesson staves are byte-identical old versus new, so grow-to-fit cannot be masking a placement bug. Verified three independent ways including raster ground truth at 4-6 device pixels per unit.

THREE CORRECTIONS FROM THE ADVERSARIAL PASS, one of them to my own number. I reported 292 clipping staves as independently verified; the real figure is 332, because my parser measured path centerlines and forgot VexFlow strokes them — the same 0.75-unit inflation the builder had found and I had missed, now reproduced three ways from the gate own output. The dead-space check would have false-fired on an author-pinned spec.height, turning a supported authoring move into a red build. And 438 text elements carry no font-size (the open-hat annotations, 14% of the corpus text) with both parsers guessing 12pt where the real inherited value is 10pt — wrong identically, safe only because the guess was larger. That correction also sharpened the blast radius: 369 of 382 frames grew on measured geometry, and 13 grew on the text estimate alone having never clipped. The gate header now states what green does NOT mean: disabling the arc sweep, the cubic stationary points or the stroke inflation each leaves it green, because the 4-unit pad absorbs anything under about 5 units.

items.title: 292 staves clip ink off the bottom of their frame today, and the gate that exists to prevent exactly this prints OK
evidence: MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED SITE, not hypothetically: 292 of 852 lesson staves draw path ink BELOW their viewBox, up to 13.88 units, and 34 draw above it, up to 20.75. check-notation-frame exits 0 on all of them.

rock-prog#0 puts two 9.2x12.1 glyphs at y 131.8-143.9 against a 130-tall viewBox. Those glyphs are the tuplet "3" numerals for its two feet triplets, confirmed invisible by rendering the same SVG with and without extra frame. A student reading that page sees two beamed eighth-note groups where the lesson means triplets, and plays the bar wrong.

fusion-half-time-shuffle#1 loses the "3" over its THIRD triplet — the one pushed higher to clear an accent — so the page prints 3, 3, (nothing), 3 over four identical triplets. On a half-time-shuffle lesson that is the single most important marking on the page. funk-purdie-shuffle#1-3, funk-modern-neo-soul#2 and fusion-metric-modulation#2 are in the same set. hi-hat-articulation#4 loses the bottom of a hi-hat-foot X notehead.

THIS IS VERBATIM THE DEFECT THE GATE WAS WRITTEN FOR. Its header says tuplet brackets "were drawn at negative y and silently clipped, so every shuffle lesson rendered without the 3 that is the entire point of the exercise (iter 31)". The same defect is live on the OPPOSITE edge.

ROOT CAUSE — the vertical half is a tautology. notation-renderer.js derives the frame from minY/maxY using the identical two regexes the gate re-runs, then pads by 4. So the gate re-checks the renderer arithmetic with the renderer own measurement — the exact anti-pattern its own header names: "Never measure the output with the thing that produced it." Across all 932 staves the y-scan finds ZERO elements outside the frame and the smallest slack it ever sees is exactly the renderer 4-unit pad. It can only fire if the grow formula is deleted, never on new content.

The horizontal half, added at iteration 68, does it properly — it parses path data with exact cubic and quadratic extremes. The fix is to give that arithmetic a y twin and compare against vy and vy+vh instead of scanning y attributes. One change also closes three related blind spots: <text> can never be caught below the frame (the scan requires both y AND height, which only <rect> has, and 247 staves carry sticking letters that hang below the stave), <line> is invisible vertically (y1/y2 do not match /\sy="/), and neither axis composes ancestor transforms.
items.acceptance: no stave draws ink outside its frame on either axis, measured by parsing path geometry rather than by re-reading the attributes the renderer used; the named examples render their tuplet numerals; the gate fails on the current code before the fix and passes after, and its coverage count is asserted rather than printed

items.title: A meter change leaves up to 500ms of the old accent pattern in flight, and sometimes that includes the old downbeat
evidence: Measured during BL-101 (iteration 75), and deliberately filed rather than folded in.

Clicks inside the scheduler lookahead are already handed to the audio clock with their accent baked in by click(), so they cannot be changed without holding a reference to every oscillator. Bound is SCHEDULE_AHEAD = 500ms; measured maximum across 14 control changes was 370ms. Stale click count is ceil(SCHEDULE_AHEAD / period): 2 at 240 BPM, 1 at 100, 0-1 at 30.
IN 4 OF 14 CHANGE EVENTS the committed click was itself ACCENTED, so the reader hears the old 1, then a short bar of 1-2 clicks, then the new 1 — measured as close as 250ms apart at 240 BPM.

The builder judgement, which the orchestrator accepted: this is legible as "I changed it, so the bar broke" in a way that an accent five clicks out of place is not. It is a rough edge rather than a lie about the beat.

PROPOSED FIX, already worked out: have click() return its oscillator, hold it on the beatTimes entry, and have setMeter stop() every entry past currentTime + ~20ms, rewind scheduledUntil to that guard, drop those entries and re-schedule. Cost is at most 2 live node references.
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: shrinking SCHEDULE_AHEAD works proportionally but trades a rare short bar for a rare DROPOUT under main-thread jank on a phone, which is worse.

The same commit window affects a mid-run TEMPO change — measured 292ms before the new period takes effect — with the same cause and the same proposed fix. The tempo path is otherwise coherent and was verified not to disturb phase.
items.acceptance: a meter or tempo change while the click is running takes effect within one click period, with no stale accent from the outgoing pattern audible after the new downbeat; no dropout is introduced under main-thread jank; verified in a real browser by reading oscillator frequencies across the change

The voice map is read from player.js and every key centre y is re-measured through the real renderer each run and asserted against the verified table. 3398 mentions, 2043 pairs, 0.8s, no build required, no new dependency.

THE VERB-SENSE RULE, WHICH THE ACCEPTANCE DEMANDED BE A RULE AND NOT A LIST. The builder established by census that "ride" is the ONLY word in the vocabulary with a verb sense anywhere in the corpus — kicks, snares, hats and chinas are plural nouns in every occurrence, confirmed independently by the critic reading all 135. So the rule has two limbs: an inflected form (rides/riding/rode) not preceded by a determiner or hyphenated modifier is the verb, which keeps "quarter-note rides only" a noun; and "ride" immediately followed by a determiner opening an object is the verb, which catches "ride the offbeats" and "surf records ride this pattern". Prepositions are deliberately EXCLUDED, because "ride on the & of 2" and "the ride on beats 2 and 4" are both nouns and including "on" would have swallowed six true sentences. Comparatives are a separate rule. All twelve KNOWN_CLEAN rows come out clean BY RULE, and the rule that cleared each one is ASSERTED rather than commented, so if any starts passing for a different reason the gate fails.

THE EXEMPTIONS, BUILT AGAINST THE ITERATION-70 FINDING THAT OVER-BROAD EXEMPTIONS ARE THE COMMONEST GATE DEFECT HERE. 20 entries, each scoped to one exercise and one voice, each tied by name to the item that will remove it, and each REQUIRED TO BE USED — an entry whose defect is fixed makes the gate fail until it is deleted, so the list can only shrink. items.title: One hedged word frees every mention of every voice in an exercise, and 127 staves are covered by nothing else

items.title: Seventy-six exercises print a swing instruction and play dead straight, including the lesson that teaches the jazz ride
evidence: MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY: 76 exercises across 27 lessons carry "swing 8ths", "swung 16ths" or "shuffle" in their meta, have no tuplets, and place notes on the subdivisions the instruction would move. That is 16 of the site 21 jazz lessons. The second lens counted 75 across 26 with a slightly narrower filter; the difference is filter width, not disagreement.

THERE IS NO SWING ANYWHERE IN THE PLAYBACK CODE. src/assets/js/pattern-math.js converts durations by pure binary subdivision ({w:4,h:2,q:1,8:0.5,16:0.25,32:0.125}, x1.5 for dots, x tuplet scale). src/assets/js/player.js contains zero occurrences of "swing". A repo-wide grep outside lessonContent.js finds the word only in prose.

jazz-ride-pattern #1-#3 — the lesson that teaches the jazz ride — are q,8,8,q,8,8 at "4/4 · swing 8ths · ♩ = 90". The skip note plays on the & instead of the last triplet partial, so it sounds like a straight-8ths rock ride.

THE CORPUS CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON ONE PAGE: all five independence-chapin-method metas read "4/4 · swing 8ths", but #4 carries 3:2 tuplets and swings while #0-#3 do not. Same in jazz-modern-jazz (#4 swings, #0/#2 do not). the-shuffle #0-#3 use real tuplets and are correct — so the site already contains both the right way and the wrong way.
The site own words define the target it misses. hi-hat-articulation#3 tip: "Treat the swing 8ths as triplets with the middle note rested out."

NOT a duplicate of BL-085, whose caveat explicitly rules the NOTATION correct and never mentions playback. The straight-eighth notation is right by convention; only the audio is wrong. This is the same shape as BL-097, where accents were inaudible until iteration 65 made them real.
items.acceptance: an exercise whose meta names a swing or shuffle feel sounds swung — either the player applies a swing ratio when the meta says so, or those specs gain tuplets the way the-shuffle already does; verified by rendering at least three of the 76 through the real player in an OfflineAudioContext and measuring inter-onset intervals against the straight baseline, and by a check asserting the two 8ths of a swung beat are not equally spaced

log.note: Filed in the iteration-79 discovery pass. Found independently by the playback lens and the curriculum lens, with matching numbers.

PROSE SURFACE WIDENED BY BL-099 CHUNK 3, recorded here rather than reverted. The five tip clauses added in iteration 80 name a swung ride — "the ding · ding-a pattern", "its jazz pattern", "the jazz pattern" — over q,8,8,q,8,8 specs with no tuplets, which is exactly the shape this item evidence cites. The metas already said "swing 8ths", so no new defect class was created and the clauses are true of the NOTATION; but five more sentences now assert a feel the player does not produce, so whoever fixes this item has five more places to check. The swing wording in fusion-coordination-foundation body was deliberately left alone as belonging to this item.

Shipped. The player swings. 76 exercises across 27 lessons — 73 at swing 8ths and 3 at swung 16ths — carried a printed feel the playback code had no concept of; player.js contained zero occurrences of the word. The fix is a data-swing attribute derived at BUILD time in .eleventy.js and never parsed in the browser, which keeps the prose parsing in the one gated place that already derives data-bpm and data-beats. Orchestrator-verified off the built site: 73 data-swing="8" plus 3 data-swing="16" across 27 pages, matching the builder count and iteration 79 discovery exactly, and pattern-math.js and metronome.js contain zero occurrences of swing or shuffle, so nothing leaked into the beat math or the click.

DOUBLE-SWING IS IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION, WHICH WAS THE RISK THAT MATTERED. Some exercises were already swung by tuplets and would have been broken by a naive fix — independence-chapin-method#4, jazz-modern-jazz#4 and all four the-shuffle exercises are correct TODAY. swungOnset is a PROJECTION rather than a warp: it moves a note only when it sits exactly on p = cell/2, and the image p = 2·cell/3 is not in that domain, so it is idempotent. Three independent layers: the build refuses data-swing for any tupleted spec; a note whose tuplet scale is not 1 is never displaced; and the projection itself. The middle layer earns its place on a case nobody predicted — a SEXTUPLET whose fourth note lands on p = 0.5 by arithmetic, which is hiphop-modern-production#1, the corpus only 6:4. The gate asserts the PROPERTY rather than the policy: its force8 cases put data-swing on tupleted specs the build refuses to mark and require those onsets to be unchanged.

THE BUILDER FOUND EVIDENCE AGAINST ITS OWN DECISION AND REPORTED IT. The ratio is a flat 2:1, justified by the site own words in four places — reading-dotted-rhythms "the long is two-thirds of a beat, the short is one-third", hi-hat-articulation#3, the-shuffle#0, and the 198 existing 3:2 tuplets that already play at 2/3. But jazz-ride-pattern own "Getting the Swing Right" section says "The ratio also breathes with tempo: swing tightens toward even 8ths as things get fast, so trust your ear over any formula" — and the builder first draft comment had claimed there was no caveat, which was false and was corrected in both files. It kept the ratio flat on one concrete ground: jazz-modern-jazz#2 and #4 are the same lesson at the same 130 BPM, one tupleted and one not, so a flat 2:1 makes them identical while any curve makes one page contradict itself at one tempo for no visible reason. Recorded as the honest weak spot: at jazz-up-tempo#2 250 BPM a flat 2:1 is deeper than that page asks for.

THREE LABELS, THREE MEANINGS, AND THE LOAD-BEARING ROW. swing 8ths moves the eighth off-beats; swung 16ths moves the sixteenth off-beats and NOT the eighths — proved on hiphop-j-dilla#2, where the sixteenths move and the eighth at 0.5 stays put. shuffle maps to the eighth division and has a population of ZERO, because every shuffle lesson already writes "8th triplets" in its meta and notates real tuplets; it is mapped rather than ignored so future content inherits the feel, and it is exercised by forcing the flag onto the-shuffle#0. The flag reads the META and not the title, and the corpus forces that: hiphop-r-and-b-basic#2 is titled "New Jack Swing Kick" while its tip says the kick "sits exactly on the second 8th of beat 2, EQUIDISTANT between the snare on 2 and the kick on 3" — a title reader would break the one exercise whose tip demands even spacing.

THE PLAYHEAD FOLLOWS, AND THE TWO AXES ARE KEPT SEPARATE. straightTime un-swings the cursor clock, so at the instant a swung eighth sounds the cursor sits at the fraction of the pattern its STRAIGHT notehead occupies — which is correct, because the notation is straight by convention (BL-085). Measured within 0.004 of the pattern at every onset. Without it every off-beat notehead would have lit up to a sixth of a beat early: 0.4167 against 0.3750 on the ride at 90 BPM, which is 125ms at 80. This is the TIME axis; BL-143 records a SPACE-axis error where VexFlow spaces noteheads by duration while progress maps to x linearly, and that is untouched — the same progress value produces the same x it always did. Durations never move either: the accumulator takes the straight length only, so patternDurationSecs and the loop point are unchanged and audit-lessons BEAT-COUNT is byte-identical.

AND IT APPLIED ITERATION 80 AUDIO LESSON WITHOUT BEING TOLD TWICE. Measuring with gain-resolved instrumentation rather than sample URLs caught that one test case hi-hat line and its PEDALED hi-hat are the same buffer — buf:8453 on all eight onsets — split 6 at gain 1.000 and 2 at gain 0.550, with the pedal beats 1 and 3 correctly unmoved. In the builder own words, a sample-URL reading would have called that one voice. That is exactly the trap iteration 80 recorded, avoided on the first attempt by the next builder.

items.title: The two kits have different internal balances, so the backbeat disappears when you switch to acoustic
evidence: Isolated single strokes, peak: hi-hat 0.4008 electronic against 1.0000 acoustic; snare 1.2404 against 0.9999; ride 0.4101 against 0.9999; crash 0.5838 in both; floor tom 0.7866 in both; bell 0.3121 in both.
SNARE-TO-HI-HAT IS 3.09 (+9.8 dB) ELECTRONIC AND 1.00 (0 dB) ACOUSTIC. In the acoustic kit the backbeat is level with the ostinato.

Cause: the five sampled voices are all normalised to full scale and play with no gain reduction, while the synthesized fallbacks keep levels tuned against each other. So in acoustic a crash is 4.7 dB QUIETER than a hi-hat and a floor tom 2.1 dB quieter — an inversion that does not exist electronically, where the crash is 3.3 dB above the hat.

Corpus consequence: 18 exercises more than double in RMS when you switch to acoustic, up to 5.39x, and they are exactly the hi-hat lessons — fusion-sixteenth#0, latin-bossa-nova#0, hi-hat-foot#1, the-shuffle#0, first-beat#0, hi-hat-articulation#0. None more than halves.

items.title: Several checks rmdir _site/dev on cleanup and delete another agent harness mid-run
evidence: Hit twice by the BL-128 builder during iteration 81, and it cost real work each time.

CONCRETE MECHANISM, located at iteration 81: check-skip-targets.js:604 does a RECURSIVE fs.rmSync on the shared _site/dev, while check-accent-dynamics, check-metro-phase and check-header-shed all use the safer rmdirSync, which fails harmlessly on a non-empty directory. A SECOND, SEPARATE FLAKINESS FOUND AT ITERATION 81 AND WORTH FIXING IN THE SAME PASS: running all 22 checks back to back in a tight loop produces transient failures across DIFFERENT checks on different runs. Observed by the orchestrator: one run failed check-swing-feel alone, a later run failed check-nav-a11y and check-notation-frame together, and every one of them passed individually immediately afterward. check-notation-frame does not even drive a browser, so this is not a headless-Edge problem — it looks like resource exhaustion from 22 node processes with no gap. items.title: check-playhead-sync.js — the cursor must drift from the noteheads mid-bar even when the audio is perfect
evidence: getMusicBounds takes startX from the first notehead and endX from lastCenter plus spacing, where spacing is the AVERAGE gap, then sweeps linearly in time.

But VexFlow allocates width by DURATION and adds width for clefs, time signatures and accidentals. So the mapping is wrong by construction and the cursor drifts from the noteheads mid-bar even when every onset is perfectly on time.
This needs no listening and no ear: compute each note sounding time from PatternMath, read its notehead x out of the built SVG, and assert playhead_x(t) lands within a few pixels of it.

RELATED TO BL-143, which owns the same defect from the space-axis side and measured a median error of 0.250 note-slots on staves that mix note values, up to 1.63, across a 24% sample. Check whether the two should merge — this item is the gate, BL-143 is the fix.
Iteration 81 established the time axis is now correct after the swing work (straightTime un-swings the cursor clock, exact at every onset within 0.004), so what remains is purely the space axis.
